title: ‘Kate & Allie’ star Susan Saint James dead at 80
summary: Susan Saint James, beloved star of "McMillan & Wife" and "Kate & Allie," died Monday at 80 after a battle with pancreatic cancer, People reported.
story: A video obituary courtesy of the Associated Press looks back at Susan Saint James’ career, including her roles in "McMillan & Wife" and "Kate & Allie."
Susan Saint James, the actress known for "McMillan & Wife" and "Kate & Allie," has died.
Saint James, 80, died Monday after a battle with pancreatic cancer, People magazine reported.

"She never met a stranger. Every person she met became the most important person in the room at that moment, from a fellow board member to the clerk at the shoe store, who usually walked away knowing her entire life story," a representative told People.

"Her defining act: weeks after losing her youngest son, Teddy, in the November 28, 2004 plane crash, she delivered his eulogy as a note to each of her other children and her husband, giving them words to heal. Even in the deepest grief of her life, she put everyone else first. Days after the crash she sat with Tim Russert to thank the people who had reached out and to tell them the family was okay."
HOLLYWOOD STARS WHO DIED IN 2026
She won a Primetime Emmy Award in 1969 for her role as Peggy Maxwell on "The Name of the Game." (Charley Gallay/Getty Images)
Susan Saint James died Monday at 80 after a battle with pancreatic cancer. (CBS/Getty Images)
"She brought that same fire and positivity to everything that followed, and never lost it," the statement continued.

Saint James began her career modeling before switching gears to television. Her breakthrough came in 1968 when she landed the role of research assistant Peggy Maxwell on NBC's "The Name of the Game." Her performance earned her a Primetime Emmy Award in 1969 and established her as one of television's rising stars.
She earned her biggest fame as Sally McMillan, the plucky wife of Rock Hudson’s San Francisco police commissioner Stewart McMillan, in the hit series "McMillan & Wife" from 1971-1976.
Susan Saint James starred as Sally McMillan on "McMillan & Wife" from 1971 to 1976. (NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images)

She left the NBC show before its sixth and final season because of a contract dispute, with her character killed off in a plane crash.
Saint James later found renewed success alongside Jane Curtin in the popular CBS sitcom "Kate & Allie," which ran from 1984 to 1989.
She is also known for roles in "Love at First Bite," "How to Beat the High Cost of Living," "M*A*S*H," "Law & Order: SVU" and "Suits."
Susan Saint James co-starred with Jane Curtin on the CBS sitcom "Kate & Allie," which ran from 1984 to 1989. (CBS Photo Archive/Getty Images)

Offscreen, Saint James was married to longtime NBC executive and former "Saturday Night Live" producer Dick Ebersol, whom she met while hosting the comedy show in 1981. The family suffered a devastating tragedy in 2004 when their 14-year-old son, Teddy, died in a private plane crash in Colorado.
She was previously married to Richard Neubert and makeup artist Tom Lucas.
Susan Saint James and her husband, Dick Ebersol, lost their 14-year-old son, Teddy, in a 2004 private plane crash. (Ron Galella/Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)

Saint James is survived by her husband, her four children – Sunshine Lucas, Harmony Lucas, Charlie Ebersol and Willie Ebersol – her seven grandchildren, and her sister, Mary Mercedes Dewey.
She is also survived by her beloved service dog, Lola.
After "Kate & Allie" ended, Saint James largely stepped away from Hollywood to concentrate on her family and charitable work, particularly her longtime involvement with the Special Olympics.

title: 'The Pitt' star Noah Wyle's 'Sexiest Man Alive' crown sparks backlash as fans fume: 'You've got to be kidding'
summary: Noah Wyle's People 'Sexiest Man Alive' crown divided fans, with critics naming Patrick Dempsey and Jonathan Bailey as better picks for the title.
story: After his Emmy win on Sunday, Wyle compared his "ER" triumph to his current success. The actor won Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series for his role in "The Pitt."
Noah Wyle has claimed the title of Hollywood's sexiest man — but some fans think People should have gone back to the drawing board.
The 55-year-old "The Pitt" star has been named People magazine's "Sexiest Man Alive" for 2026, sparking a social media debate over whether the longtime TV heartthrob was the right man for the title.
"Out of all of the people in the world…this is who you pick? You’ve got to be kidding," one critic fumed.
NOAH WYLE, MATT DAMON, LEONARDO DICAPRIO STILL CAPTIVATING AUDIENCES WELL INTO THEIR 50S
Noah Wyle's new title as People's 2026 "Sexiest Man Alive" has fans divided, with some celebrating the Hollywood veteran and others questioning the magazine's choice. (Jeff Lipsky/PEOPLE)
Another took a swipe at Wyle’s competition, writing, "Not even the sexiest in that show."
And one commenter wasn’t about to let the announcement slide without a pun.
"More like Noah WHY-le! Ha ha but no seriously who’d you actually pick?" the user joked, while another asked, "is this a joke?"
"Poor Noah. I like him. Good actor but he’s not sexiest man alive. Come on," another wrote.
"Not bad... not great..." one person assessed.
Noah Wyle appears on the cover of People magazine's "Sexiest Man Alive" issue. (Jeff Lipsky/PEOPLE)
The criticism came alongside plenty of support for Wyle, whose journey from "ER" favorite Dr. John Carter to leading man of "The Pitt" has brought him back into the spotlight.
Noah Wyle is turning heads — and raising eyebrows — after landing People's coveted "Sexiest Man Alive" crown at 55. (Jeff Lipsky/PEOPLE)
"Thank you for getting it right finally!" one fan declared.
"This is actually an incredible win for anyone who grew up watching ER. why did it take Hollywood this long to give him the crown," another wrote.
MATT DAMON SAYS HOLLYWOOD'S 'RUTHLESS' NATURE HAS TAKEN HIM AWAY FROM FATHERHOOD MORE THAN HE'D LIKE
One admirer argued that Wyle brings more to the table than a handsome face, writing, "#NoahWyle does not just have the looks. He's the whole damn package. That's why he's The Sexiest Man Alive!"
"Just accept we have a 55-year-old as the Sexiest Man Alive! Noah Wyle, just know that you’re hot!"
"I thought that sounded like a prank — just not in a million years did I think that this would be an honor bestowed on me," Noah Wyle told People of their decision. (Jeff Lipsky/PEOPLE)
Other social media users suggested alternative candidates.
"they could’ve just had patrick dempsey do it again if they wanted someone older," one commenter suggested.
Another backed a different contender, writing, "@Deancain would have been a good choice. Just saying."
And for fans still mourning last year's winner, one person offered a simple solution: "it’s not too late to choose jonathan bailey again."
Patrick Dempsey, Dean Cain and Jonathan Bailey were thrown out by some social media users as better options for the title. (Stefanie Keenan/WireImage; Paul Archuleta; Mauricio Santana)
For Wyle, the "Sexiest Man Alive" title marks another milestone in his Hollywood comeback.

The actor first became a household name as Dr. John Carter on "ER," spending years at the center of one of television's defining medical dramas before making his final appearance on the series in 2009.
Noah Wyle's career comeback on "The Pitt" has earned him critical acclaim. (Jeff Lipsky/PEOPLE)

Years later, he returned to the medical drama genre as Dr. Michael "Robby" Robinavitch in "The Pitt," winning the Emmy for outstanding lead actor in a drama series in both 2025 and 2026 and introducing himself to a new generation of viewers.

Off-screen, the 55-year-old is a husband and father of three who has spoken candidly about the pressures of fame, his devotion to his family and his support for healthcare workers.
Wyle has three children — Owen and Auden from his first marriage to Tracy Warbin, and Frances with his wife, Sara Wells, whom he married in 2014.
Noah Wyle as Doctor John Carter in "ER." (Chris Haston/NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images)
Wyle himself admitted the honor caught him off guard.

"I thought that sounded like a prank — just not in a million years did I think that this would be an honor bestowed on me," he told People editor-in-chief Charlotte Triggs in an exclusive cover interview.

His wife, Sara, was more enthusiastic, encouraging him to embrace a title he initially struggled to believe was real.

"She was very pleased that this reflects well on her taste," Wyle said. "She thinks I’m a good guy and that the kind of person that I am and the kind of father I am, the kind of husband I am, is worth promoting. I thought, ‘Okay, if you say so.’"
His children also had some concerns.
Wyle told People magazine that his wife was "very pleased" with his new title. (Stefanie Keenan/Getty Images for The Daily Front Row)
Wyle said his son immediately worried about the unwanted attention that could come with the new title.

"My son is super practical. He was like, ‘Oh, this is going to make my life so much harder now. But that’s cool, Dad. But also, you invite a lot of haters too.’ My older daughter was just like, ‘No way, no way.’ Because I think she’s going to tease me about this for the next 50 years."

title: Rob Riggle says Hollywood work is disappearing from LA: 'It's the exception now'
summary: Rob Riggle reveals why actors are fleeing Los Angeles as work dries up and shares his dream of moving back to his native Kansas City someday.
story: The "Christmas at the Kringles" actor told Fox News Digital he'd like to move back to the Midwest someday.
Rob Riggle said many people in the industry are leaving Los Angeles because the work has moved away.
The comedian, who stars in the upcoming holiday horror film "Christmas at the Kringles," told Fox News Digital that getting a job in the city is more the exception than the rule now.

"I think a lot has changed, the way things are done," he explained. "I used to be out here because I needed to be available to work here. A lot of the work isn't here anymore. I mean, a lot of it, the work is not here anymore. It's the exception now, if you get to work here. So that's one reason."
HOLLYWOOD STAR SOUNDS ALARM OVER DISAPPEARING JOBS AS PRODUCTIONS FLEE CALIFORNIA
Rob Riggle said that industry work is moving away from Los Angeles. (Variety via Getty Images)
Riggle said that actors don’t even need to be in L.A. to audition anymore.

"They don't even do that anymore. Like you don't get to go in anymore," he said. "You have to put yourself on tape standing in front of a white, opaque wall in your garage, trying to make a selfie video, reading with your neighbor, you know, or whoever's in the house, you know? It's terrible. It's just a terrible way to do business. And for whatever reason, that's what we get after COVID. So that's the new paradigm and it sucks."

"I used to be out here because I needed to be available to work here. A lot of the work isn't here anymore."

Rob Riggle stars in the new comedy-horror holiday film "Christmas at the Kringles." (Victoria Sirakova/Getty Images)

title: Meghan Markle's acting comeback suffers major blow as Netflix 'safety net' disappears: expert
summary: Meghan Markle is no longer in talks to join "The Gentlemen" as sources allege Netflix leaked casting news to boost the show's publicity online.
story: Doug Eldridge, founder of Achilles PR, explains why Meghan Markle may need to break from her public image and take on unexpected acting roles to revive her acting career.
Meghan Markle is no longer in talks to join "The Gentlemen," with friends alleging she was "used to help promote" the Netflix series.

Royal experts told Fox News Digital that the Duchess of Sussex's "safety net" with Netflix "is gone" as uncertainty surrounding her relationship with the streaming service threatens to derail her acting comeback before it even gets off the ground.

"Harry and Meghan's champion inside Netflix, Bela Bajaria, has recently left the streaming service," British broadcaster Helena Chard told Fox News Digital. "The previous safety net is gone. Unfortunately for Meghan, she may want to jump straight into a top acting role, but there is far more stacked against it happening."
MEGHAN MARKLE’S ACTING RETURN COULD SPARK FRESH PROBLEMS WITH PRINCE WILLIAM, KATE MIDDLETON: EXPERT

Meghan, Duchess of Sussex speaks onstage during the 2025 TIME100 Summit at Jazz at Lincoln Center on April 23, 2025, in New York City. Sources close to the duchess told The Telegraph she is no longer in talks to join "The Gentlemen" on Netflix. (2025 Getty Images)
Variety reported Bajaria was leaving Netflix after nearly 10 years with the company. According to the outlet, around 1,000 employees were laid off.
Bajaria was leaving Netflix after nearly 10 years with the company.
"What I find most revealing is that Meghan's camp now appears comfortable publicly criticizing Netflix," Kinsey Schofield, host of "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," told Fox News Digital.
Bela Bajaria, then-chief content officer at Netflix, attends the 31st annual Screen Actors Guild Awards at Shrine Auditorium and Expo Hall in Los Angeles, on Feb. 23, 2025. (Getty Images)

"This was one of their most important commercial partners. You don't typically throw a company under the bus when you're counting on them to finance your next big project. To me, this is the clearest indication yet that their relationship with Netflix has effectively come to an end."
WATCH: MEGHAN MARKLE NEEDS A HOLLYWOOD REINVENTION, PR EXPERT SAYS

The Duchess of Sussex was reportedly under consideration for a role in the third season of Guy Ritchie's Netflix drama following her move back to the U.K. with Prince Harry. However, sources close to Meghan have accused Netflix of leaking news of her potential involvement to boost publicity for the show.
"Some people in her camp feel she was used to help promote Season 2, because they knew it wasn't as good as the first season and had already commissioned a third," one source told The Telegraph.
Theo James attends "The Gentlemen" U.K. series global premiere at the Theatre Royal in London on March 5, 2024. (Anadolu via Getty Images)

"It's the oldest marketing trick in the book: get a big name to read a script, then leak that you're 'in conversation' with them when, in reality, nothing is particularly far along. The whole thing left a bit of a sour taste in the Sussex camp's mouth. Needless to say, Netflix got what it wanted: huge viewing figures for Season 2 and a lot of publicity."
Meghan Markle’s return to acting comes after a series of post-royal ventures, including her Netflix lifestyle series, "With Love, Meghan." (Getty Images)
Fox News Digital reached out to Archewell and Netflix for comment.
Schofield told Fox News Digital she wouldn't be surprised if Meghan's relationship with Netflix had soured.
Meghan Markle's As Ever spread is seen here. (As Ever)

"Netflix has already withdrawn from its investment in As Ever," Schofield said. "Meghan herself credited Bajaria with recognizing the television potential in her homemade gifts. She told the TIME100 Summit that 'With Love, Meghan,' her lifestyle show, was Bajaria's idea."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Meghan Markle is reportedly eyeing a return to acting after years spent building a new identity outside the royal family. (Tommaso Boddi/Getty Images)

"Now, after Bajaria's departure, we're hearing accusations that Netflix exploited Meghan for publicity," Schofield said. "Does that sound like a relationship with a promising future? I suspect Meghan's camp feels comfortable criticizing Netflix because there's nothing left to protect."
A source close to Netflix has pushed back on the accusations, telling The Times, "This is not a show in need of stunt casting."
Guy Ritchie attends "The Gentlemen" Season 2 world premiere at Guildhall on Sept. 2, 2026, in London, England. (Getty Images)
A Netflix consultant who worked closely with Bajaria told The Times that Meghan and Harry's relationship with the streaming service has been called into question.
Meghan Markle was previously the host of a lifestyle series on Netflix titled "With Love, Meghan." (Jake Rosenberg/Netflix © 2025)

"Effectively, their biggest champion has gone, and they are uncertain about who will be shouting for their cause in the future," the source said. "Teams at the company were well aware of how she was fiercely loyal to the couple and determined to prove they were a successful signing, even when the response from viewers was different."

"The Gentlemen," which is set in the U.K., was renewed for a third season in August. Deadline previously reported that talks about Meghan joining the cast were in the "very early stages," while The Hollywood Reporter reported that the role "is currently being written, so it's unclear how many episodes she would appear in."
Meghan Markle on the red carpet for "Suits," circa 2015. (Mike Coppola/NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images)

British royal expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital that Meghan "did nothing to thwart all the speculation" sooner, noting that Netflix also did not issue a statement to address the casting rumors.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's Hollywood dreams are in jeopardy as they face a brand crisis over collapsed deals and fading public interest, according to royal experts. (Aaron Chown/PA Images)
"They benefited from the additional coverage even if, as they claim, it wasn't needed," Fordwich said. "Such a high-profile show would have been a high-profile win for Meghan."

In March 2026, Netflix and Meghan announced the end of their partnership involving her lifestyle brand, As Ever, with the Duchess of Sussex moving forward independently. As Ever launched in 2025, about a month after the premiere of "With Love, Meghan." The show released two seasons and a holiday special in 2025. Reports in January 2026 indicated that it would not return for a third season.
Meghan Markle, a former American actress, became the Duchess of Sussex when she married Prince Harry, a British prince, in 2018. (Ben Stansall-WPA Pool/Getty Images)

Harry and Meghan first partnered with Netflix in 2020 under a deal reportedly worth $100 million. Their projects included the 2022 series "Harry & Meghan" and "Live to Lead," 2023's "Heart of Invictus" and 2024's "Polo." Although reports in July 2025 suggested the original agreement would not be renewed, Netflix announced a new multiyear, first-look deal with Archewell Productions in August 2025.

Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, Nicole Avant, and Ted Sarandos attend Netflix's "BEEF" Season 2 Montecito Tastemaker at a private residence on April 10, 2026, in Montecito, California. (Stefanie Keenan)

According to The Times, Netflix previously scrapped an animated project from the couple, while little has been reported about their planned film adaptations of the war memoir "No Way Out" and the romance novels "Meet Me at the Lake" and "The Wedding Date."

It is unclear whether Netflix will pick up a potential documentary about Harry's late mother, Princess Diana, ahead of the 30th anniversary of her death in 2027. People magazine reported that Harry is exploring projects, but no documentary has been finalized or confirmed.

Diana, Princess of Wales, wearing a cream lace gown with a scalloped neckline designed by Murray Arbeid and the Lover's Knot diamond and pearl tiara, smiles as she attends a dinner at the British Ambassador's Residence in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 11, 1985. (Getty Images)

"'The Gentlemen' is an established Guy Ritchie production with its own audience," Schofield said. "The suggestion that Netflix needed Meghan to rescue its viewing figures is quite a claim from someone whose own lifestyle series struggled to become a mainstream hit."

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle returned to the U.K. six years after leaving for California. (Getty Images)
"Meghan's royal connections might get her into the room, but they don't guarantee her a successful acting career. At some point, the work has to speak for itself."

Before marrying Harry in 2018, Meghan played Rachel Zane in "Suits" for seven seasons. In 2022, Meghan told Variety that she was "done" with acting. She has since filmed a cameo in the upcoming film "Close Personal Friends," which stars Lily Collins and Jack Quaid.

Alysa Nahmias and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, attend a special screening of Roadside Attractions' "Cookie Queens" at AMC The Grove 14 in Los Angeles on July 28, 2026. (Roadside Attractions via Getty Images)

Sources told People magazine that Meghan and Harry have been discussing her return to acting "for some time." The outlet reported that Meghan is "excited" about returning to the profession and is exploring opportunities.
Meghan Markle attends the Womenswear Spring-Summer 2026 show during Paris Fashion Week on Oct. 5, 2025, in Paris, France. (Andrea Cremascoli/Getty Images)

"Meghan Markle has repeatedly told us she was finished with acting," Schofield said. "During her 2017 engagement interview, she said she'd 'ticked this box.' Now, after six years in Hollywood and several attempts to reinvent herself, she's now reportedly entertaining a return to the profession she so confidently walked away from. Sure, a role in an established Guy Ritchie production would have given her an opportunity to change the conversation about her professional accomplishments. But I also think the timing of the story is revealing."
Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, attends the Balenciaga Womenswear Spring/Summer 2026 show during Paris Fashion Week on Oct. 4, 2025, in Paris, France. (Getty Images for Balenciaga)

"Harry and Meghan had just returned to Britain, a move that could easily be interpreted as an acknowledgment that their Hollywood ambitions hadn't worked out," Schofield said. "Suddenly, we're hearing about Meghan's potential acting comeback. The Sussexes seem determined to turn every bit of publicity into a much larger PR strategy. The problem is that their PR ambitions continue to outpace their professional accomplishments."
Royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner believes Meghan's desire to return to acting, whether in Hollywood or the U.K., is genuine.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Actress Meghan Markle visits AOL Studios in New York City on March 17, 2016. (FilmMagic/Getty Images)

"The role which brought her to fame in ‘Suits’ proves she is an actress of quality," he said. "If she wanted to return to acting, which I believe is still a passion, then she could bring great credit to any production."
Bajaria's departure amid layoffs at Netflix raises further questions about the future of Harry and Meghan's projects with the streaming service.
Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, participates in a Scar Tree Walk in Melbourne, Australia, on April 16, 2026, during a four-day visit with the Duke of Sussex. (Asanka Ratnayake/Getty Images)

"I suspect Harry and Meghan recognized that their Hollywood experiment wasn't delivering the success they expected," Schofield said. "Their return to Britain gives them something Los Angeles can't offer — proximity to the monarchy."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Brooke Hogan blasts ‘fake, greedy people’ after Hulk’s Florida home sale: ‘Enjoy your dirty money’
summary: Brooke Hogan accused unnamed friends and family of exploiting Hulk Hogan for profit after his Clearwater Beach mansion sold for $5.9 million.
story: HGTV "Rock the Block" contestant Brooke Hogan details the emotional fallout of her relationship with her late dad, Hulk Hogan, sharing how his absence still shapes her drive.
Brooke Hogan is lashing out at the "fake, greedy people" she claims profited from her late father Hulk Hogan as she mourns the sale of the wrestling legend's Florida home.

Last week, Hulk's 5,400-square-foot, beachfront mansion in Clearwater Beach sold for $5.9 million after it was originally listed for nearly $11 million in January, according to TMZ. The outlet also reported that the neighboring guest cottage sold separately for $2.8 million.
Hulk, who was born Terry Bollea, died at age 71 in July 2025 after suffering cardiac arrest at his home in Clearwater Beach. The WWE icon's cause of death was later determined to be a heart attack.
NICK HOGAN HELPS GUIDE HULKAMANIA INTO FUTURE WITH SPORTS BAR OUTSIDE MSG, SHARES THOUGHTS ON FATHER'S LEGACY

In a series of emotional posts shared to her Instagram Stories Monday, Brooke reflected on losing the home where she shared memories with her father while accusing unnamed friends and family members of exploiting him for their own gain.
The 38-year-old TV personality also took aim at what she described as "dirty money," claiming some people only appeared "at the end" of her father's life "to collect."
"The sick feeling is indescribable," Brooke wrote in one post alongside a photo of the house with a red and white SOLD sticker at the top.
Brooke Hogan slammed "fake, greedy people" after the sale of her late father Hulk Hogan's home.  (K Mazur/WireImage)
"This house was where dad and Jen envisioned growing old together," she added, referring to Hulk's ex-wife Jennifer McDaniel, to whom he was married from 2010 to 2021.
NETFLIX DOCUMENTARY DIRECTOR ON HULK HOGAN'S TRUMP SUPPORT AND THE BACKLASH THAT FOLLOWED HIM TO THE END
"Where we brought him back to…surgery after surgery," Brooke continued. "Pool days. The smell of gasoline in his garage. His workouts downstairs."

"We cooked, we watched Jerry springer, we played music, we cried," she recalled. "I walked in that garage every visit and hugged him right when he’d open the garage door. I’d sit next to him for hours in the chair he died in."
Hulk's 5,400-square-foot, beachfront mansion in Clearwater Beach, Florida sold for $5.9 million after it was originally listed for nearly $11 million in January. (AFP via Getty Images)
KRISTIN CAVALLARI SAYS SHE LEARNED A PAINFUL $250K LESSON INVOLVING HER FATHER AT 22
"His whole environment, his energy, his work, his relationships: First Jen — who no one but me treated with respect. Then I was gone…the truth teller… I’m sure to everyone’s delight."
"And now it’s all gone. Sold for profit. Just like him…used for f-----g everyone else’s gain. Saddest ending I’ve ever seen. You know who TF you are," Brooke concluded.
KRISTIN CAVALLARI CUT FATHER OUT OF HER LIFE AFTER HE CROSSED ‘MAJOR LINE’ INVOLVING HER KIDS
Hogan shared her emotional reaction to the sale in several Instagram posts. (Brooke Hogan/Instagram)

In another post, Brooke uploaded an image in which she was seen posing with Hulk a dock outside the house, writing, "Let’s not forget who was there for the 15 years before the vultures swooped in conveniently."

Brooke went on to share a series of photos documenting the years that she spent by her father's side, writing that she "adored," loved and "cherished" him. She also posted images of pill bottles that were labeled with Hulk's name, noting that she "tracked every med."
CRYSTAL HEFNER FELT 'ABSOLUTELY BRAINWASHED' DURING HUGH HEFNER MARRIAGE, REVEALS STRICT PLAYBOY MANSION RULES
The "Brooke Knows Best" star also recalled how she and McDaniel helped care for Hulk during his health struggles.
Brooke blasted "vultures" who she said profited from Hulk. (Brooke Hogan Instagram )
"Jen and I were the nurse crew. Notebooks, records, prescription pickups, overnights, switching shifts," Brooke wrote.
"This woman spent more time in the trenches than ANY of us did," she continued. "He LOVED her dearly. And she loved him."
"She wanted to be there till his last breath despite the trauma she endured that I witnessed..," Brooke added.
OZZY AND SHARON OSBOURNE'S LONGTIME LOS ANGELES HOME HITS THE MARKET FOR $17M AFTER HIS DEATH AT 76
Brooke claimed that McDaniel "asked for nothing" following her split from Hulk. She wrote that McDaniel could have "fought for money" but instead "vanished" without launching a "smear campaign."
Describing McDaniel as "hilarious," Brooke recalled the two having "girl days" together. She praised her former stepmother as "pure love and grace."
"Their breakup was devastating for me," Brooke wrote. "I loved her, but I knew my dad was in the best care with her too."
"DEVOTION was an UNDERSTATEMENT," she added.
Brooke heaped praise on Hulk's ex-wife Jennifer McDaniel. (WireImage)
Alongside photos of Hogan recovering from surgeries, Brooke recalled how she and McDaniel repeatedly accompanied him to the hospital.
"We did surgery… after surgery… after surgery," she wrote.

In one photo, Brooke pointed out blood on McDaniel's shirt and missing fingernails. She posted images of Hulk standing in the hospital room, writing, "I'm taking the photo. You see anyone else there? Whole room… no one else?"

Brooke then shared a photo that was taken during a July 2025 episode of "WWE SmackDown!" following Hulk's death. In the photo, WWE stars, several wrestling legends and production crew were seen gathered onstage for the traditional 10-bell salute in memory of Hulk.
Brooke also shared a photo that was taken during WWE's tribute to Hulk on "Smackdown!" (Brooke Hogan Instagram)
"Not ONE of these people stayed longer than an hour in the hospital… if they even showed," Brooke wrote.

"And I’ve had to hear everyone say I’m the jerk for stepping away from the toxic behavior and brainwashing, fake, greedy people… ‘I should have been there.’ ‘Everyone else’ was there till the end. NO. They were there AT the end. To collect," she wrote on a photo of herself with Hulk.
Brooke shared another image of the Hulk's home, writing, "Enjoy your dirty money. You took my dad."
However, Brooke later pushed back against reports that interpreted her posts as an attack on WWE stars, insisting that was not her intention.
DISGUSTING TROLLS ATTACK HULK HOGAN'S DAUGHTER FOR STARTING EMOTIONAL POST ABOUT DAD WITH A BIKINI PICTURE
Brooke recalled memories from spending time with Hulk at his Florida home. (Brooke Hogan Instagram )
"Hey reporters: I don't have beef with the stars of WWE. Nor did I say that. Do your job right or don't do it at all," she wrote in a follow-up post on her Instagram Story.
Brooke explained that she was criticizing people who she said "show up to public tributes" despite not supporting her father privately when she was "in the trenches with him."
"But they'll show up to get their face on camera," she wrote, adding, "That includes so called ‘friends' AND family."

In another post, Brooke elaborated on her accusations as she blasted unnamed people who she claimed "only visited him if he payed [sic] for it" and others who "got a paycheck if they pretended they were his friend."
She also called out "the 'yes men' who were too afraid to protect him with truth" and "the ones who promised me they'd do the right thing when he died."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
"Apparently EVERYONE will show up at the end if you're famous enough and they can profit off your demise," Brooke concluded.
The two, who were once extremely close, were estranged at the time of Hulk's death.  (Brooke Hogan Instagram )

Brooke and Hulk were once extremely close and their father-daughter relationship was a major part of their reality series "Hogan Knows Best," which ran from 2005 to 2007. However, their relationship became complicated over the years and Brooke was estranged from Hulk during the final two years of his life.

In July 2023, Hulk amended his will to exclude Brooke and her descendants, leaving her brother Nick as the sole beneficiary of his probate estate. The "Rocky III" star shared Brooke and Nick, 36, with his ex-wife Linda Hogan. Hulk was married to Sky Daily from 2023 until his death.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Brooke said her posts were directed at unnamed friends and family.  (Brooke Hogan Instagram )

Brooke has maintained that her estrangement from Hulk was not due to a single falling-out. After Hulk died, Brooke said she ultimately stepped away following a series of "respectful disagreements" with her father that took an emotional toll on her.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Hulk never publicly addressed his estrangement from Brooke or his decision to formally remove her from his will. However, a source told Us Weekly in March 2025 that the wrestling icon had told people he did not know why his daughter had stopped speaking to him. Brooke later said she had asked to be removed from his will because she wanted no part of an anticipated battle over his fortune.

"I just know how my family is," Brooke told TMZ in August 2025. "I've seen how certain members of my family go after money. And I see how they fight over money. And how they turn on each other over money."
Ashley Hume is an entertainment journalist for Fox News Digital and Fox Business who covers breaking news, celebrity culture, major industry events and the business of entertainment.

title: Jon Gosselin claims he's 'perfect strangers now' with six of his kids after years of no contact
summary: Jon Gosselin reveals he hasn't spoken to six of his eight children in years, calling them "perfect strangers" amid Collin Gosselin's memoir.
story: ‘In the Shadow of Eight’ author tells Fox News Digital about his alleged childhood abuse and isolation.
Jon Gosselin hasn't spoken with most of his children in more than a decade.

The reality star, who appeared on "Jon & Kate Plus 8" before his divorce from ex-wife Kate Gosselin, admitted that his strained relationships with six of his kids have made them "perfect strangers now."
When Entertainment Tonight asked about the last time Gosselin spoke with most of his children, he admitted, "I haven't talked to them."
KATE GOSSELIN CALLED A 'MONSTER' IN SOCIAL MEDIA COMMENTS AFTER SON COLLIN ANNOUNCES MEMOIR
Jon Gosselin admitted he hasn't spoken to most of his children in more than one decade. (Tommaso Boddi)

TLC aired "Jon & Kate Plus 8" from 2007-09, when the former couple divorced. One year later, the show was rebranded as "Kate Plus 8," which focused on her life following the split, and ran until 2017.
Jon and Kate – who have twins Mady and Cara and sextuplets Hannah, Leah, Alexis, Joel, Aaden and Collin — announced their divorce in a broadcast episode of the show.
Collin and Hannah began living with Jon in 2018, when Jon admitted that while Collin went "no contact" with his siblings, Hannah was still speaking with her mother.
'JON & KATE' STAR COLLIN GOSSELIN CLAIMS MOTHER ZIP-TIED AND LOCKED HIM IN BASEMENT ROOM AS A CHILD

Collin Gosselin claimed his mother, Kate Gosselin, had him institutionalized against his will. (Michael Simon)

Jon and Kate Gosselin share eight children together. They divorced in 2009. (Amy Sussman)
HAYDEN PANETTIERE AND THE CHILD STARS WHOSE RELATIONSHIPS WITH THEIR MOMAGERS TURNED COMPLICATED

title: Natalie Portman says being sexualized as a child star forced her to become a 'good girl' as protection
summary: Natalie Portman reveals how she built a "good girl" persona to counter childhood sexualization in Hollywood and why it became a lasting trap.
story: James Sexton, Esq., explains how emotional withdrawal develops between couples, and why renewed attention, affection and mindfulness can reveal whether both partners remain invested.
Natalie Portman learned early that growing up in Hollywood meant protecting herself from the very image that made her famous.

The Oscar-winning actress opened up about the lasting impact of being sexualized as a child star, revealing how she carefully crafted a "good girl" image to shield herself from unwanted attention – only to find that the persona followed her well into adulthood.
Portman began her career in films featuring dark themes, such as 1994 thriller "Léon: The Professional," "Heat" and "Beautiful Girls."
BELLA THORNE SAYS HOLLYWOOD TREATED HER LIKE A KID ON SCREEN AND AN ADULT OFF CAMERA
Natalie Portman said she adopted a "good girl" persona as a child star to protect herself from being sexualized in Hollywood. (Patrick Camboulive/Sygma)

As Portman navigated the pressures of Hollywood at a young age, she and her parents made a deliberate effort to separate her on-screen persona from who she was in real life. Rather than embrace the provocative image associated with some of her early roles, Portman maintained a more reserved public image. She chose conservative, age-appropriate clothing for red carpet appearances while remaining focused on her education and academic success.

"I think there was a conscious effort, because I was depicted as this sexualized Lolita, that I wanted to be like, ‘No, I’m serious, I’m a good girl, I’m a prude, I’m smart, I’m a student,’ emphasizing that as almost a safety mechanism," she told Harper's Bazaar.

As her career progressed, Portman continued to gravitate toward complex, emotionally demanding roles. She eventually earned an Oscar for her performance in "Black Swan" and another nomination for "Jackie."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Natalie Portman won an Oscar for her performance in "Black Swan." (James Devaney/WireImage)

But as her career flourished, Portman found that the serious image she had carefully cultivated, coupled with the demanding roles she continued to play, created a lasting misconception about her personality.

"But then, over time, it became like everyone thinks I’m really serious," Portman noted. "I’m very silly, and I love to laugh more than anything, and I love to goof off. People always think I’m a perfectionist, I think, because of 'Black Swan.' I’m the opposite. I’m forgiving with myself. In college, we had a phrase: ‘Done, not good.’"
After spending much of her career exploring darker, more complex characters, Portman said her priorities have shifted toward bringing audiences a sense of happiness.
Natalie Portman said she's focusing on bringing more joy to audiences after years of portraying darker, emotionally complex characters. (Dominique Charriau/WireImage)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"Right now, it’s a lot of joy," she told the outlet of the current phase of her career. "I think it’s both for myself and what I hope to offer an audience, because it just feels … I mean, every time has dark moments, but it feels like there’s a lot of really heavy stuff going on. It’s just ever-present in our face, and so it does feel like the biggest service you can do right now as an artist is to deliver some joy."

Portman has also found joy in her personal life, recently welcoming a child with her partner, Tanguy Destable. A few weeks after welcoming her third child, Portman told Harper's Bazaar she's been "full of wonder and joy at this magical little human."

title: Eric Bauza, 'Looney Tunes' voice actor behind Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, dead at 46
summary: Eric Bauza, the voice actor who carried on Mel Blanc's legendary "Looney Tunes" legacy, died Sunday at age 46 of hypertensive cardiovascular disease.
story: Bauza shares what it means to be such a big part of the Looney Tunes legacy & director Dave Green talks about creating the adventure, which in theaters this week following Wile E. Coyote suing Acme for all the faulty gadgets.
Eric Bauza, the voice behind iconic "Looney Tunes" characters including Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, has died, Fox News Digital has confirmed.
Bauza died Sunday from hypertensive cardiovascular disease, according to the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. He was 46.

Beginning in 2001, Bauza amassed more than 400 voice-acting credits in a career that gave voice to beloved characters in animated Looney Tunes series including "Puss in Boots," "Muppet Babies," "Avatar: The Last Airbender," and countless others.
The voice actor's family confirmed his death on Instagram, but has not shared any additional details.
HOLLYWOOD STARS WHO DIED IN 2026
Eric Bauza attends the "Space Jam: A New Legacy" party on June 29, 2021. (Matt Winkelmeyer/Getty Images)
Fox News Digital reached out to Bauza's representative.
Bauza's early breakthrough came when he voiced Stimpy in the 2003 series "Ren & Stimpy: Adult Party Cartoon," taking over the character previously voiced by Billy West.
He became one of Hollywood's most recognizable voice talents, particularly for his work carrying on the legacy of legendary Looney Tunes performer Mel Blanc.

"I’m a fan first when it comes to this franchise, this band of characters. Mel Blanc will always be the original gangsta, the godfather of voiceover," Bauza told Fox News Digital back in 2020. "He was the first voice actor credited on screen as a voice actor. They never did back in the day. And we’re talking about the ‘30s and ‘40s."

Eric Bauza voiced several iconic "Looney Tunes" characters, including Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, and appeared in films such as "Space Jam: A New Legacy" and "Coyote vs. Acme." (Eric Charbonneau/Getty Images)

"So he really paved the way to show the importance of vocal performance, not an on-camera one. And the fact that we’re sitting here now talking about his performance just shows you how incredible, impactful and influential his sound is."

Bauza's Looney Tunes work included feature films such as "Space Jam: A New Legacy" (2021), "The Day the Earth Blew Up: A Looney Tunes Movie" (2024) and this year's "Coyote vs. Acme." Bauza won three Children's and Family Emmy Awards during his career.

Beyond bringing Bugs Bunny to life on screen, Bauza had a deep appreciation for the character's roots and what made him so beloved by generations of fans. Reflecting on Bugs Bunny's signature personality, Bauza once explained how the character's unmistakable New York accent came to be.

Eric Bauza once explained that Bugs Bunny's signature accent was inspired by a combination of Brooklyn and Bronx accents, a creative decision made by original voice actor Mel Blanc. (Kevin Winter/Getty Images)

"And if you’re wondering where [Bugs Bunny] got that accent from, they say he’s a rascally rabbit," Bauza told Fox News Digital. "So [Mel] thought, he’s gotta be a tough character. And there’s no one tougher than a New Yorker, that’s what he said. He said it’s either Brooklyn or The Bronx. He mixed the two together, those accents. So that’s why he kind of has that street talk."

"I think he represents the everyman, the every rabbit," he added. "He doesn’t have a lot of high demands in life. All he wants is a carrot and a nice afternoon where no one bugs him. And if you get on his bad side, that’s when you gotta look out. That’s when he becomes the trickster. But really, he’s just a simple rabbit, nothing to him. I think that’s why he’s so appealing. And I think that’s why when he gets in trouble, people want him to succeed."

His work helped keep some of animation's most enduring characters alive for modern audiences.

title: Michael Douglas doesn't 'feel bad' about affair revelations from 'before Catherine'
summary: Michael Douglas revealed Catherine Zeta-Jones just got his memoir two days before his podcast appearance, joking their 25-year age gap softens the blow.
story: In his memoir, "One Helluva Ride," the actor admitted he had an affair with his "Basic Instinct" co-star, Jeanne Tripplehorn. (This video contains AI-assisted content.)
Michael Douglas gave a cheeky response when asked how his wife, Catherine Zeta-Jones, had reacted to his new tell-all, "One Helluva Ride."

The 82-year-old actor's new memoir, published Oct. 6, contained revelations about his life, including his secret affairs with his former co-stars Kathleen Turner and Jeanne Tripplehorn, as well as his past cocaine use and struggles with addiction.
During an appearance on the "Happy, Sad, Confused" podcast on the day of the book's release, host Josh Horowitz asked Douglas whether Zeta-Jones, 57, knew "everything" that he revealed in the book.
MICHAEL DOUGLAS GETS EXPLICIT ABOUT HOW HE FILMED SEX SCENES BEFORE INTIMACY COORDINATORS
"I'll be home to ask her because she just got the book two days ago. I told her this was all, as I say, B.C., before Catherine," Douglas said in the interview, which was published on Oct. 19.
Michael Douglas admitted that he "doesn't feel bad" about his wife Catherine Zeta-Jones reading about his affair revelations in his memoir. (Getty Images for The Red Sea International Film Festival)
"And you know, we have a 25-year age difference, so I'm looking at some of these films, like with Kathleen, and Catherine would have been seven years old," he joked.
"I don't feel bad," Douglas added. "I think she understands."
Michael Douglas and Catherine Zeta-Jones married in 2000. (Axelle/Bauer-Griffin/FilmMagic)

In "One Helluva Ride," Douglas confirmed that he and Turner, 72, had an affair in 1983 while filming the hit 1984 romantic adventure movie "Romancing the Stone," a rumor they denied for over 40 years.

At the time, Douglas was legally married to Diandra Luker, with whom he shares son Cameron, though he said in his memoir that they were separated when production on the film began, and they were both having extramarital affairs.
Douglas recalled that he and Turner continued to deny rumors that they were romantically involved during production of the sequel and even years later when they reunited on "The Kominsky Method."

Douglas joked that Zeta-Jones would have been "seven years old" when he and Kathleen Turner had an affair while filming "Romancing the Stone." (20th Century-Fox/Getty Images)

"The truth is that during the production of ‘Romancing the Stone,' Kathleen and I fell hard for each other and began a relationship," he wrote. "It wasn’t a fly-by night affair; it grew naturally from how closely we were working together, how much pressure we were under, how much we respected and cared for one another, and how attracted we were to each other. Like every other guy in the world at the time, I was knocked sideways by Kathleen."

He noted that he and Turner kept their affair a secret for 40 years to protect Luker and Cameron. Douglas wrote that the two decided to end their relationship after Luker visited them on set with Cameron "and made it clear to her [Turner] that we were still married."

After reports circulated about Douglas' admission, Turner said in a statement to People, "Good heavens, what a fuss about something 40 years ago! I love Michael, and I look forward to enjoying the book."
Michael Douglas and Diandra Luker were married for 23 years, from 1977 until their divorce was finalized in 2000. (Sygma via Getty Images)
SHARON STONE SAYS SHE 'NEARLY DIED' AFTER 'BASIC INSTINCT' OPENED THE DOOR TO HOLLYWOOD'S DARK SIDE
Douglas also disclosed that he and Tripplehorn, 63, who was almost 20 years his junior, had an affair during the filming of their 1992 movie, "Basic Instinct."
"The truth is, I fell very hard for Jeanne despite our nearly 20-year age difference," he wrote. "In fact, I was ready to officially leave my wife for Jeanne. I was crazy about her."
Douglas also revealed that he had an affair with Jeanne Tripplehorn. (TriStar Pictures/courtesy Everett Collection)
Douglas recalled that his "relationship with Jeanne lasted through production," but that they "went our separate ways" once production ended.
"But I will always think of her as an amazing actress and a truly terrific woman that I was very fortunate to spend time with," he added.

Douglas maintained that he and Luker were still separated at the time. Luker filed for divorce in 1995, and their split was finalized in 2000.

Tripplehorn has not publicly commented on Douglas' memoir, though the actor previously said she approved of him including their relationship in the book. During an interview with Page Six, Douglas said, "I talked to her before I put it in the book," adding that "she was fine" with it.

title: Christian singer Natalie Grant urges fans not to 'ignore your body' after fall led to emergency surgery
summary: Natalie Grant reveals how a fall outside a restaurant led to kidney bleeding, an ICU stay and emergency surgery that could have ruptured her bladder.
story: The Christian singer told Fox News Digital about the time she tripped while on the way to dinner and suffered internal bleeding.
Christian singer Natalie Grant is opening up about a crazy health scare.

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 54-year-old singer discussed what it meant to her to honor Dolly Parton at the Dove Awards and how she ended up in the hospital with internal bleeding.

Grant explained that after moving her daughter into her dorm room at college, they went out to dinner together with her husband, and on the way, her foot "caught this brick on the ground" and she "belly flopped" onto the ground.

"I thought, 'Oh, maybe I broke a rib' or 'Man, that's gonna leave a bruise' or 'I kind of knocked the wind out of me,'" she said. "But then I got up and I kept walking to dinner. I'm like, I'm sore, but I'm gonna be okay. It wasn't until I realized that I was bleeding internally. And when I realized that it was an emergency, got to the emergency room. And they were like your bladder could rupture, because my kidney was bleeding, and I wasn't able to pass urine."
Grant shared how a simple fall on the way to dinner led to internal bleeding. (Jason Kempin/Getty Images)

She explained that when she initially arrived at the emergency room, doctors "were kind of confused about what was going on," and it wasn't until she was admitted into the ICU when they realized how serious her condition was.

"I had a catheter so you could see the blood kept filling. I wouldn't stop bleeding, and I think that's when they were like we've got to get you in for surgery and figure out what's going on. But they all let me know like if you wouldn't have come in, like I talked about maybe going to a bigger hospital, and they said, 'No you were really smart to come as fast as you could and get here as quickly as you can,' because if I didn't, my bladder would have actually ruptured, and I wouldn't have known it."

The singer went on to say that even through all her pain, she was thinking about her children and how they were feeling, noting that as moms, "we're always concerned about everybody around us," even when bleeding internally.

While in the hospital, she was thinking of her daughter in the hospital with her, who "faints at the sight of blood," as well as her other two daughters back home in Nashville, and how she was going to tell them.
Grant urges her fans to listen to their body when they feel pain. (Tibrina Hobson/Getty Images)

"I was in pain, but I didn't want to miss the moment. I was like, 'No, we are celebrating the fact that she has finished college, and we are going to dinner together, and we're going to make this memory,'" she said. "And I'm kind of like hurting and limping and not able to fully eat my meal. And I was, like, I don't think I can ignore this anymore, but that was just such a picture of what moms do."
After her incident, Grant urges her fans not to "ignore your body," saying, "God created our body in such a way that it gives us signs" and too often, those signs go ignored until "it's too late."
WATCH HERE: CHRISTIAN SINGER NATALIE GRANT IS 100 PERCENT HEALED FROM HER INTERNAL INJURIES SUSTAINED AFTER A FALL
Months after the fall, Grant said she has completely healed, and that, "funnily enough," she did actually break a rib in the fall, and that has been the most painful part.
WATCH HERE: DOCTORS WERE INITIALLY CONFUSED WHEN NATALIE GRANT CAME INTO THE HOSPITAL AFTER HER FALL

"I just last week had my final cystoscopy which checked inside my kidney and my bladder and everything looks fantastic. It's 100 percent healed. You actually can see a scar from where it was and there's I'm like, there's a sermon in that. It's all healed, we still have the scar, but it's healed. And then I just had an ultrasound as well. So internally, everything is 100%. And I just, I thank God because that could have gone 100 different directions. But I'm very, very grateful for good medical care and for the faithfulness of God took care of me."

Amy Grant and Natalie Grant honored Dolly Parton at the Dove Awards. (TBN/Trinity Broadcast Network)

The Christian singer recently honored Dolly Parton at the Dove Awards earlier this month, telling Fox News Digital "the most emotional moment for me came in the planning season of it."
The 57th Annual GMA Dove Awards took place on Tuesday, Oct. 6, 2026, at Nashville's Bridgestone Arena, hosted by Tauren Wells.

When putting together the tribute, Grant was left wondering how to honor someone who made such an impact in not just the music industry, but the world, noting, "I'm not gonna sing nine to five or some of her greatest hits, like how do we make this work?"

"And it was really in looking and reading and remembering and knowing the story of Dolly's faith and how much her faith mattered to her, guided her, led her to the way she lived her life, to the ways she loved people, to the fact she was sure of who she was," she said. title: Prince Harry making 'big mistake' that could destroy chance of royal reconciliation: expert
summary: Prince Harry told GQ he wants peace with his family, but royal experts say his public interviews are thwarting any chance of reconciliation.
story: Royal broadcaster Ian Pelham-Turner argues King Charles must take action to bring Prince Harry and Meghan Markle back into the royal fold amid family tensions.
Several royal experts believe Prince Harry is making a "big mistake" that could ruin his chances of reconciling with his family.

In his first major interview since returning to the U.K. with his family, the Duke of Sussex told GQ he wants to make peace with his father and brother. However, royal commentator Richard Fitzwilliams told Fox News Digital that Harry's willingness to publicly discuss his strained family relationships only makes the royals more reluctant to extend an olive branch.

"The peace offering is already undermined as it is public," said Fitzwilliams. "That continues to be his big mistake. He cannot be trusted. [The Sussexes] had already launched brutal attacks on the royal family [with their tell-alls]. Family disputes are bitter. But numerous interventions from 'friends' and interviews like Harry's in GQ make this highly unlikely."
PRINCE HARRY SAYS ‘MOST IMPORTANT THING IS TO RECONCILE’ WITH ROYAL FAMILY

Prince Harry sat down with GQ for an interview recorded in New York in late September 2026 and published Oct. 20. The Duke of Sussex spoke about grief, the death of his mother, Princess Diana, fatherhood, his family's return to the U.K. and his desire to reconcile with his father, King Charles III, and brother, Prince William. (2026 Max Mumby/Indigo)

Speaking about the family rift, Harry told GQ: "Some people don't want it to work out. I want it to work out. With everything else that's going on in the world, the most important thing is to reconcile — that's the key point."

"Scars stick around forever," Harry continued. "But what your perception is, and what your mindset is to those things that have happened, letting go of the past. That’s something that I would encourage everybody to do: If there’s certain things from the past that are still affecting you every day, that’s harder to let go of. But, for me, there’s enough drama in the world and enough drama in people’s lives to continue with issues with family."
Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, arrives for a visit to the Community Recording Studio in St. Ann's on Sept. 9, 2025, in Nottingham, England. (Getty Images)
Harry also told GQ that he has been "really criticized" for sharing his side of the story.

"I find it fascinating because everybody else is allowed to tell their version of my story, but God forbid I should be able to tell the other side of it."

Royal broadcaster Helena Chard told Fox News Digital that although Harry may yearn for reconciliation after years of the Sussexes publicly airing their grievances, "the palace doesn't trust Harry and Meghan." Chard said Harry's decision to speak publicly "proves Prince William's fear — anything said in private will end up in print."
Prince Harry's book "Spare" seen displayed in a bookstore on Dec. 16, 2023, in Bath, England. (Matt Cardy/Getty Images)
"Vindication on Megxit and absolution without apology do not equate to reconciliation," Chard added.
Prince Harry told the BBC in 2025 that he's ready for reconciliation. (Samir Hussein/WireImage)

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex stepped back from their roles as senior royals in 2020, citing intense media scrutiny and a lack of support from the palace. After moving to California that year, the couple discussed their struggles in interviews and documentaries. Harry's 2023 memoir, "Spare," further strained his relationship with the royals. Several experts told Fox News Digital that Harry and William are still not on speaking terms.
Office workers in London watch the Duke and Duchess of Sussex's "Harry & Meghan" docuseries on Netflix on Dec. 8, 2022. (Jonathan Brady/PA Images via Getty Images)

"Following conversations with the duke, the queen has written confirming that in stepping away from the work of the royal family it is not possible to continue with the responsibilities and duties that come with a life of public service," Buckingham Palace said in a statement on Feb. 19, 2021.
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle returned to the U.K. six years after leaving for California. (Getty Images)
In response, the couple issued a statement of their own, saying: "We can all live a life of service. Service is universal."
Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, poses for a selfie with well-wishers after a visit to Community Recording Studio in Nottingham, central England, on Sept. 9, 2025. (POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

"In short, their position is akin to private citizens with commercial and charitable interests," the letter added.
Prince Harry and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, arrive at the Endeavour Fund Awards at Mansion House in London on March 5, 2020. Soon after, the couple moved to California. (Justin Tallis/AFP)

Another friend of the couple told The Times that Harry and Meghan "hate" the phrase "working members of the royal family."

Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex are seen greeting members of the public at the Cruising Yacht Club of Australia on April 17, 2026, in Sydney, Australia. (Cameron Spencer/Getty Images)

title: Donna Mills, 85, draws the line at unexpected OnlyFans request: ‘I’m not going to’
summary: "Knots Landing" star Donna Mills revealed the one surprising everyday activity she refuses to film for her OnlyFans subscribers.
story: Donna Mills tells Fox News Digital what changed her mind about joining the platform — and why she says there's no pressure to bare it all.
"Knots Landing" star Donna Mills is revealing the one unexpected request she refuses to fulfill for her OnlyFans subscribers.

During a Friday appearance on ABC's "Nightline," the 85-year-old actress told correspondent Kayna Whitworth that her content largely consists of glimpses into her daily life but asserted that there is one routine she won’t perform for the camera.

"I do the Peloton," Mills said. "Just, you know, they’re the things of everyday life: having a cup of coffee, you know. They say they like it when you brush your teeth…I’m not going to brush my teeth."
Donna Mills revealed the one OnlyFans request that she won't fulfill. (Disney via Getty Images)
DONNA MILLS DOES 100 SIT-UPS A DAY, PLAYS TENNIS FIVE TIMES A WEEK AT 85 BUT WON'T QUIT DORITOS
When asked if she believes that most of the OnlyFans users who are engaging with her are men, Mills said, "I think so. Yeah. Sometimes you don’t know."

While Mills drew the line at brushing her teeth on camera, she appeared more open to sharing racier content with her subscribers. However, she explained that she does not believe full nudity is necessary to be sexy, pointing to one of her past Playboy shoots as an example.
PLAYBOY'S CELEBRITY-DRIVEN RELAUNCH FACES CREDIBILITY TEST IN ONLYFANS ERA, EXPERT SAYS
The "Knots Landing" star said she plans to sell never-before-seen "Playboy" photos. (2005 CBS WORLDWIDE INC.)
"I think it’s sexier to be not just totally naked, you know," she said. "And have a little imagination about it."
"One of the pictures in ‘Playboy,’ which I think is one of the sexiest things, is me in the shower, in a dress," Mills added.
CRYSTAL HEFNER FELT 'ABSOLUTELY BRAINWASHED' DURING HUGH HEFNER MARRIAGE, REVEALS STRICT PLAYBOY MANSION RULES
The "Play Misty for Me" star said she believed that the never-before-seen "Playboy" outtakes could be particularly enticing for her OnlyFans subscribers.
"I think the probably the most appealing would be the ones that weren't in the magazine, right?" she said. "Because they're from the shoot, the same shoot, but they weren't in the magazine."
'HARRY POTTER' ACTOR SAYS ONLYFANS VIDEOS EARNED HER MORE THAN HER ENTIRE ACTING CAREER
After Whitworth asked how much she might charge subscribers for one of the previously unseen photos, Mills floated a potential price.
Mills launched her OnlyFans page in July. (2024 Getty Images)
"Boy, I'm not sure," she said. "Maybe I'm not sure — $100."
"$100?" Whitworth replied.
"More?" Mills asked.

"We're thinking you could go up a little higher," Whiteworth told her.
Mills surprised her fans when she announced that she had launched an OnlyFans account in July.

The actress, who became a television sensation playing the glamorous and ruthless Abby Cunningham on "Knots Landing" from 1980 to 1989, said the platform would give her a chance to connect with fans in a more personal way.
Mills said fans were hungry for a behind-the-scenes look at her life, which she noted wasn't possible during her TV heyday.
Mills said she shared a glimpse at her daily life with her subscribers.  (Photo by Michael Tullberg/Getty Images)
'KNOTS LANDING' STAR DONNA MILLS ISSUES URGENT WARNING ABOUT AGING

"They want to know me," she told Variety at the time. "They want to know what I do during the day when I’m home. They want to see my home. They want to know much more about my personal life than we ever experienced back in the ’80s and the ’90s that, you know, the fans were cut off from."

"I've always appreciated the incredible support and encouragement I've received from my fans over the years," Mills said. "Social media has been a wonderful way to stay connected, but I'm excited to join OnlyFans because it offers the opportunity for a more personal and direct connection,"
However, Mills emphasized that she planned to approach OnlyFans on her own terms.
"It’s simply another platform to spend quality time with the people who’ve supported me throughout my career while staying true to who I am," she said.
Andy Bachman, CEO of Creators, Inc., the talent agency that manages Mills' OnlyFans account, noted that the Hollywood veteran isn't switching up her image.

"This is not about changing who she is. It is about giving her longtime fans more access to the personality, style and behind-the-scenes moments they already love," Andy Bachman, CEO of the talent agency Creators Inc., said.
The actress is reportedly making "many six figures." (© 2025 Disney. All rights reserved.)

"Donna has always been fearless and ahead of her time," Bachman added. "She told me, 'YOLO — let's do it,' and that perfectly captures her attitude. She is approaching OnlyFans on her own terms and creating a space that feels authentic, personal and completely true to her."
During an appearance on "TMZ Live" shortly after launching her account, Mills said that she wasn't planning to pose nude but didn't entirely rule out the possibility.
"Who knows? My first answer would be, oh, no, I won’t do that," she said. "But then my second answer is, I don’t know."
"I don’t want to do anything that’s salacious, you know what I mean?" Mills added. "That isn’t my personality. That isn’t what I feel good doing. But if it’s cute and sexy … we’ll see."
In August, Mills appeared on "Creators Inc. Podcast," less than a month after launching her account. At the time, Bachman, who hosts the podcast, shared an update on her page's performance.
"I can say that you are doing incredibly well," he said. "Many six figures, and it’s been early."
Bachman noted that Mills had already received some unusual requests, including "foot kink people" who asked to see the actress "stomping on grapes" with her bare feet in her vineyard.
"I’m gonna do it," Mills said. "I tried to shoot it myself. But you can’t shoot something while you’re stomping, it just doesn’t work."

"I'm going to uh… I'm going to do that very soon… and do it right so that you know people can… really enjoy it," she continued. "I think it's really funny and fun and uh it's the kind of thing that I want to be able to share with the fans."

Mills teased that her page will be "spicy." (GC Images)
Mills also explained that part of her motivation for launching her OnlyFans was to prove that getting older doesn't mean life gets smaller.

title: Brandi Glanville says doctors are 'taking my face off' in exploratory surgery after years of health issues
summary: Brandi Glanville details the $5,000 exploratory surgery to remove what she believes is something alive moving beneath the skin on her face.
story: Reality star Brandi Glanville explains why her recent financial strain made turning down opportunities more difficult and pushed her to prove she could perform again on FOX's "Special Forces."
Brandi Glanville is taking a major step in her ongoing health battle by going under the knife.

During an episode of her "Brandi Glanville Unfiltered" podcast, shared on Thursday, Oct. 22, the 53-year-old reality star went into detail about the "exploratory surgery" she is scheduled to have on Friday.

"Dr. Carlo Honrado is taking my face off on Friday and going to do an exploratory surgery to kind of do a power wash under my skin," she said. "And then he knows where there's two definite spots, like either fungal balls or something alive. I think it's alive personally cause it moves when it wants."

She explained that after four years of dealing with the issue, she is "super excited" but also "scared to death" because she has "never had facial surgery" and has heard the procedure is "more intensive than a facelift."
Glanville shared that she is undergoing "exploratory surgery." (Paul Archuleta/Getty Images)
FORMER REALITY STAR OPENS UP ABOUT NEW DIAGNOSIS AFTER YEARS-LONG HEALTH ORDEAL

While she is nervous, Glanville is hopeful the surgery will be a success, as facial plastic and reconstructive surgeon, Dr. Honrado, "comes highly recommended." She noted that she is "okay" with the $5,000 price tag, telling herself, "what if he actually does take it out and it's done?"
"It started in my face, my cheek and my jawbone, and then it went over my head back in my neck. Now it's down my spine," she explained.
She went on to say that the doctor told her if he is able to "cut that head off the beast", getting rid of the rest of it will be more manageable.
Glanville previously shared that she believed she picked up a parasite after visiting Morocco in 2023. She suffered from facial paralysis and was initially diagnosed with stress-induced angioedema.

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the "Real Housewives of Beverly Hills" alum revealed she agreed to compete on the current season of "Special Forces" because she needed the money after years of spending on medical treatments.

title: Country star Cody Johnson says Nashville wanted to change him before success
summary: Cody Johnson walked away from a Nashville record deal after executives told him to ditch his cowboy hat, then spent a decade proving them wrong.
story: Cody Johnson talked to Fox News Digital on the iHeartRadio Music Awards carpet, and admitted his pre-show ritual is "pretty simple."
Nashville wanted Cody Johnson to ditch his cowboy hat before giving him a shot at country music stardom.

The Texas-born country star said he walked away from a record deal after executives suggested he swap his signature cowboy look for a baseball cap — a move he viewed as a demand to change who he was before he could make it in the music business.

"They wanted a baseball cap, which I have nothing against, but it was the approach. It was the 'you're great, but once we change you, you'll make it.' And it pissed me off," he said in an interview with "CBS Mornings." "I tipped my hat and said, 'Thank you for your time.'"
CARRIE UNDERWOOD SAYS HER FAMILY COULD BE 'SELF-SUSTAINED' ON TENNESSEE FARM AWAY FROM HOLLYWOOD SPOTLIGHT
Cody Johnson performs onstage during the 61st Academy of Country Music Awards at MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas, on May 17, 2026. (John Shearer/Getty Images for ACM)
It was a gamble that could have cost him his shot at stardom.
Instead, Johnson spent the next 10 years building a career on his own terms, playing bars and honky-tonks before becoming one of country music's biggest stars.
During his interview, Johnson spoke candidly about his rise to fame and the years of work behind his success.
COUNTRY SINGER CODY JOHNSON FORCED TO STOP 'GOD BLESS AMERICA' PERFORMANCE AS VIOLENT BRAWL BREAKS OUT
Long before arena crowds and industry recognition, the singer was a small-town Texas kid who dreamed of becoming a rodeo star.

Country music star Cody Johnson revealed he walked away from a Nashville record-label opportunity after executives pushed him to trade his signature cowboy hat for a baseball cap. (Mary DeCicco/MLB Photos via Getty Images)
He eventually traded bull riding for music after years of injuries and setbacks and selling CDs in rodeo parking lots as he tried to build a following.
The country star also struggled to believe his ambitions were within reach.

"Truthfully, in my core, I didn't feel I was capable of attaining a goal that big, you know, to be a huge country music star, to own a cattle ranch," Johnson said.
Cody Johnson refused to compromise his cowboy image to satisfy Nashville executives, choosing to build his country music career on his own terms. (Jason Kempin/Getty Images)
After turning down the label opportunity, he spent years playing small venues, struggling financially and spending long stretches away from his family to keep his career alive.

Country singer Cody Johnson spent a decade performing in bars and honky-tonks before achieving mainstream success without abandoning his traditional cowboy style. (Christopher Polk/Dick Clark Productions via Getty Images)

title: Rob Lowe gets candid about his best on-screen kiss as other major stars dish on their worst
summary: Rob Lowe called Nastassja Kinski his best on-screen kiss, while Nicole Kidman roasted Alexander Skarsgard over a falafel-fueled smooch scene.
story: During an appearance on "Nostalgia Tonight with Joe Sibilia," the "Seinfeld" star recalls filming romantic scenes with Carol Burnett, revealing the actress's playful joke. He also reflects on other unforgettable TV legends.
Celebrities are getting real about their best and worst on-screen smooches.
Rob Lowe recently praised one of his former co-stars as the best on-screen kiss of his career, while Nicole Kidman previously roasted one of her former screen partners as her worst.
Whether it was the circumstances surrounding the shoot, the chemistry between the actors or a co-star's choices at lunch, these star's share what can make or break a romantic scene for them.
Here are some stars who have disclosed their best and worst on-screen kisses.
Rob Lowe
Lowe said Nastassja Kinski was his best on-screen kiss. (Clark Clifford/The Hollywood Reporter via Getty Images)
Rob Lowe dished on the actress he considers to be his best on-screen kiss.

During a recent appearance on "Watch What Happens Live," the "The Outsiders" star told host Andy Cohen while playing "Plead the Fifth" that his best kiss was with co-star, Nastassja Kinski, while filming "The Hotel New Hampshire."
"Have a look at her," he said when asked what made her the best. "At that moment in time, she was probably the most beautiful woman I’d certainly ever seen."
While she was his favorite co-star to kiss, he also mentioned he felt "very, very scared" to kiss her.
Sharon Stone
Robert De Niro and Sharon Stone having a tender moment as they lay on a bed in a scene from the film 'Casino', 1995. (Photo by Universal Pictures/Getty Images) (Universal Pictures/Getty Images)
Sharon Stone has only one co-star in mind when it comes to her best kiss.

During an interview on  SiriusXM’s "Radio Andy" in April, the actress called Robert De Niro, "the best kisser in the business," and said the kiss they shared while filming the 1995 movie, "Chicago," "really just knocked me out."

"We did this scene where I have to go to the bathroom, and because I play this hustler, I get him to give me money to go," Stone explained. "He gives me this money and I look at him like, ‘Really? I think a little more than $50 for the bathroom.' And he … reaches in, and he gives me, like, $100, and then I lean over, and I kiss him."
ROBERT DE NIRO GETS EMOTIONAL AS AMY POEHLER PRAISES HIM FOR SPEAKING 'TRUTH TO POWER' AS REGULAR TRUMP CRITIC

The kiss was enjoyed by both her and De Niro, with Stone telling Andy Cohen that when director, Martin Scorsese, asked if they wanted to film the scene again, "We both looked at him and went, 'Yeah, I think maybe we need one more.'"
Sylvester Stallone
Stallone said his kiss with Talia Shire was the worst in his career. (Sunset Boulevard/Corbis via Getty Images)
Although fans love the kiss between Rocky Balboa and Adrian in "Rocky," Sylvester Stallone doesn't have fond memories from filming the scene.
In a recent interview with Page Six Hollywood, Stallone referred to his kiss with actress Talia Shire as "the kiss from hell," but it was no fault of the actress.

"Then I go in to kiss her — pull the hat off, the glasses — and… her nose is running. Badly," he said. "So we go in for the kiss and she goes [bad coughing noise]. And I go, ‘Oh my God!’And I have to keep moving forward. There is no reverse. So I knew exactly as soon as I kissed her that within an hour I had the flu."
He then recalled that shortly after filming the romantic scene, he found himself in bed with a runny nose.
Nicole Kidman
Kidman said Skarsgard is her worst on-screen kiss because he ate falafel before filming the scene. (Dan MacMedan/Getty Images)
Nicole Kidman did not hold back when it came to describing her worst on-screen kiss.

During an appearance on the "Las Culturistas" podcast in March, the "Practical Magic" star revealed she "cannot stand bad breath," calling it a "dealbreaker" for her when it comes to men. She noted, "You want me to lean in? Smell good."
She then called out her former "Big Little Lies" co-star, Alexander Skarsgard, for eating a falafel shortly before they were going to film a romantic scene.

"I'm like, 'No, no, no, Alex. I'm meant to be kissing you and into you. Put away the falafel now. Because the bad breath does not turn me on,'" she recalled. "I said, 'No more falafel. Nope. Not before you kiss. Not before you make love. No more falafel. Put the falafel away.'"

Kate Hudson

Kate Hudson has been very honest about how she feels about her on-screen kisses with many of her former co-star's.

While playing Vanity Fair’s Lie Detector Test with her "The Glass Onion" co-star, Janelle Monáe, Hudson was asked to compare her on-screen kisses with two former co-stars; Billy Crudup and Matthew McConaughey.

"I think Billy is a gentler kisser," she said. "Better? I wouldn’t say better. Definitely…definitely just gentler. It’s a more sophisticated version of a kiss...It’s like theater, Stanislavski, and like Longhorns."
Hudson was then asked about her kiss with Dane Cook she quickly replied, "No. Canceled." She starred with him in 2008’s "My Best Friend’s Girl."

"The thing is, every time I kiss McConaughey, it's like there's just something happening and there's like snot or wind," she laughed. "When we were kissing in the end of 'Fool's Gold,' we're like in the ocean, we had the plane crash. He just had snot all over his face."
When speaking with Monáe, she confirmed that her favorite on-screen kiss was with Liv Tyler, saying "She has the softest lips of them all."

PAT SAJAK MAKES RARE PUBLIC APPEARANCE AFTER STEPPING AWAY FROM 'WHEEL OF FORTUNE'

title: 'Baywatch' star David Chokachi credits 3 am wake-ups, twice-daily workouts for unbelievable physique at 58
summary: David Chokachi reveals the Andrew Huberman-inspired ice plunge and 3:30 a.m. routine that got him camera-ready for his return to "Baywatch."
story: David Chokachi, 58, told Fox News Digital that the new "Baywatch" cast couldn't believe his insane figure.
David Chokachi is in the best shape of his life thanks, in part, to an unconventional routine.
Chokachi, 58, wanted to "make a statement" when he returned to the "Baywatch" set nearly 30 years after he first appeared on-screen as beloved lifeguard Cody Madison.

After climbing out of a dark place following an arduous recovery process due to Achilles tendon ruptures, Chokachi said that he "found a higher operating system" within, and became hyper-focused on optimizing his brain chemistry to benefit both mental and physical health.
'BAYWATCH' STAR BRANDY LEDFORD SHARES FITNESS SECRETS AT 57, SAYS SHE'S 'NOT READY TO HANG UP MY BIKINI YET'
David Chokachi admitted he's more fit now than when he worked on the original "Baywatch." (Getty Images; Clint Brewer/Backgrid)

"I'm up at 3.30 in the morning every day and ready to go. My body's like, 'It's time to go,' and everybody thinks I'm insane, but it's my dream window of time, I love it," Chokachi told Fox News Digital.
He cited neuroscientist Andrew Huberman's approach to health as an influence on his own routine and noted that former Navy SEAL DJ Shipley also helped shape his mindset.
WATCH: 'BAYWATCH' STAR DAVID CHOKACHI CREDITS EARLY-MORNINGS, TWO-A-DAY WORKOUTS FOR PEAK FITNESS
Shipley "found this program of stacking micro wins, which are the little things you do, but you do them every day, and you recognize them, like, 'OK, that was a win,'" Chokachi said.
