title: Former rival dodges full-throated El-Sayed endorsement after bitter Senate primary
summary: Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., who lost to El-Sayed in the Democratic primary, said she's 'on the team' but declined to say she was fully behind the Michigan Senate nominee.
story: Michigan Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens discusses why she has not campaigned alongside Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed during an appearance on CNN's "State of the Union." (Credit: CNN "State of the Union" - Oct. 25)

Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., repeatedly stopped short of saying she was "fully behind" Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed when pressed on national television Sunday, months after he narrowly defeated her in a bitter primary and just days before the midterm elections.

CNN's Dana Bash first pressed Stevens on why she has yet to campaign alongside El-Sayed despite endorsing him after the primary. Stevens responded by pointing to her work campaigning for Democratic House candidates across Michigan.
But when Bash later asked directly whether she was "still fully behind" El-Sayed, Stevens again stopped short of saying yes.
MICHIGAN DEMOCRAT HALEY STEVENS BACKS EL-SAYED AFTER NARROW PRIMARY DEFEAT, CALLS SOCIALISM ‘DANGEROUS’
Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., a candidate in the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate in Michigan speaks to supporters election night Tuesday, Aug. 4, 2026, in Detroit. (Paul Sancya/AP Photo)
"Look, I'm on the Democratic ticket," Stevens said. "I can't say that I agree with everything that's gone on."
Stevens instead highlighted her support for Democratic gubernatorial nominee Jocelyn Benson and House candidates, but not El-Sayed.
Bash pointed out that she had not mentioned him.
"Well, look, I would just say you asked me if I'm still on the team," Stevens responded. "I'm on the team."
HALEY STEVENS URGES EL-SAYED TO DITCH HASAN PIKER AFFILIATION AFTER MICHIGAN PRIMARY

Rep. Haley Stevens of Michigan, right, and former Wayne County Health Department Director Abdul El-Sayed are facing off in the August 4, 2026, Democratic Senate primary in the Great Lakes battleground state. (Evan Cobb for The Washington Post via Getty Images; Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

The exchange underscores lingering tensions inside the Michigan Democratic coalition following a contentious Senate primary that exposed divisions over Israel, Iran and the direction of the party. Stevens' supporters included constituencies El-Sayed has been working to consolidate behind his campaign, particularly Black and Jewish voters, as he faces Republican Mike Rogers in the general election.
Stevens also suggested Sunday that El-Sayed has more work to do with some of the voters who backed her in the primary.
BLACK VOTERS RIP DEMS OVER TAKING THEM FOR GRANTED IN EL-SAYED'S BACKYARD: ‘HUSH US UP’
Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed speaks to reporters on the campaign trail in Lansing, Michigan. (Fox News Digital/Paul Steinhauser)

When asked whether El-Sayed had done enough to reach her former supporters in Michigan's Black and Jewish communities, Stevens pointed specifically to outreach she had urged him to make to Black voters.
"I had said to, you know, the coordinated campaign, I'm like, hey, give a speech in the Black community, right?" Stevens said.
"But yeah, I mean, that didn't happen," she added. "That speech hasn't happened."
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

El-Sayed is facing former Republican Rep. Mike Rogers in the closely watched race to succeed retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters, with the Michigan seat central to the battle for control of the Senate.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The contest has emerged as a test of the Democratic Party's progressive wing, with El-Sayed campaigning on policies including Medicare-for-all and an end to U.S. military aid to Israel, while Rogers has sought to portray him as outside Michigan's political mainstream.
Alec Schemmel is a Politics Reporter for Fox News Digital who is originally from Charlotte, North Carolina but now resides in the Washington D.C.-Baltimore Metro Area.

title: Cuban exile-turned-congressman unloads on Dem Senate hopeful over Cuba remarks
summary: Cuban-American Rep. Carlos Gimenez blasted Florida Democrat Angie Nixon over her Cuba remarks after CBS News apologized for mischaracterizing her response.
story: Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla., breaks down her worries about Florida Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Angie Nixon, her record and the key issues shaping the race ahead of the midterm elections on 'Hannity.'

EXCLUSIVE: A Cuban-American congressman whose family fled Cuba's communist regime slammed Florida Democratic Senate candidate Angie Nixon, accusing her of not going far enough in condemning the island nation's dictatorship.

Nixon, the Florida state representative running to unseat Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla., pushed back after CBS News initially characterized her remarks during an interview aired Monday as a refusal to call Cuba a dictatorship.
"Do you consider that Cuba is a dictatorship?" the interviewer asked Nixon.
"That is what people have told me. I have never been to Cuba, and so I will have to take their word for it," Nixon, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), responded.
FLORIDA SENATE CANDIDATE ANGIE NIXON CALLS FOR JAILING GOP OPPONENT ASHLEY MOODY

Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., campaigns with Democratic U.S. Senate candidate, Florida state Rep. Angie Nixon, during a Fighting Oligarchy Tour campaign stop at The Cuban Club Courtyard on Oct. 17, 2026 in Tampa, Florida.
In a now deleted tweet, CBS accused Nixon of refusing to answer the question, which Nixon responded to as "a serious failure of editorial reporting."

"To claim I declined to answer the question is categorically false. That is not journalism. It is misinformation," Nixon added in her online response. CBS has since re-uploaded the footage on X and apologized for the misleading language.
However, Rep. Carlos Gimenez, R-Fla., whose family fled Cuba when he was young, told Fox News Digital that he still believes Nixon refused to acknowledge the island nation's regime.

"There is no ambiguity: Cuba is a communist dictatorship that has imprisoned, tortured, and murdered innocent people for decades," the congressman said. "Floridians deserve leaders who stand unequivocally for freedom, not politicians who whitewash the horrors of communism."
Cuba has been under communist rule since 1959.
RUBIO WARNS CUBA HAS INFILTRATED US WITH SPIES, CALLS COMMUNIST REGIME AN 'ESPIONAGE SUPERPOWER'
Ian Vallecillo, a South Florida lawmaker whose family escaped the totalitarian regime in Nicaragua, echoed Gimenez's claim in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"This is a perfect example of ideological cognitive dissonance. Acknowledging Cuba’s dictatorship means confronting the failure of a Marxist system she appears sympathetic to," the lawmaker stated. "Cuba is a nearly 70-year experiment in Marxism that has produced economic devastation, repression, and a brutal dictatorship. Yet these are the same people who constantly accuse Trump and Republicans of being dictators, while hesitating to acknowledge actual dictatorships that align with their ideology."

Vallecillo accused Nixon of "showing her true colors," who has a biased view of communist regimes since she and her fellow DSA members have spent "their lives defending a failed ideology and therefore cannot recognize that they are on the wrong side of history."
RNC WARNS DEMOCRATS FACE 'POLITICAL SUICIDE' AFTER DSA PRAISES FIDEL CASTRO, DEMANDS RUBIO'S PROSECUTION
Rep. Carlos Gimenez, R-Fla., speaks during the Congressional Hispanic Conference press conference in the U.S. Capitol on March 25, 2025. (Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc. via Getty Images)
Nixon did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

During her interview, Nixon criticized the decades-long U.S. embargo on Cuba and expressed support for returning to policies implemented under former President Barack Obama, arguing that such an approach could help address the island's widespread blackouts and shortages of medical care.
In 2014, Obama began a diplomatic thaw with Cuba, restoring diplomatic relations and easing certain economic and travel restrictions imposed during the Cold War.
RUBIO URGES CUBANS TO WORK WITH CIA TO BRING POLITICAL CHANGE TO COMMUNIST-RUN ISLAND
The Obama administration also removed Cuba from the State Department's list of state sponsors of terrorism in 2015 and eased restrictions on certain forms of trade with the island nation.
Nixon and other DSA members have long argued that the U.S. embargo contributes to the deteriorating living conditions faced by the Cuban people.
CUBA’S DICTATORSHIP HAS LONG BEEN A THREAT TO AMERICA. NOW, IT’S FINALLY TEETERING

President Donald Trump’s administration has maintained that certain U.S. sanctions target businesses tied to Cuba's military, including Grupo de Administración Empresarial S.A. (GAESA), a conglomerate controlled by the Cuban armed forces.

President Barack Obama and Cuban President Raul Castro visit during an exhibition game between the Cuban national team and the Major League Baseball team Tampa Bay Rays at the Estadio Latinoamericano, March 22, 2016, in Havana, Cuba. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)
According to reports, GAESA is worth over $14.5 billion and oversees 37% of the country's gross domestic product.

"That's not sanctions on the Cuban people. The Cuban people don't benefit from GAESA," Secretary of State Marco Rubio said.

title: Hundreds of staged armed robberies helped thousands pose as crime victims in US immigration scam: DOJ
summary: Parth Nayi organized hundreds of staged armed robberies at Chicago-area businesses to help noncitizens fraudulently apply for U visas in exchange for cash.
story: Republican Congressman Chip Roy discusses the alarming visa fraud scheme involving 10 Indian nationals who staged armed robberies to exploit immigration laws. Roy introduces the PAUSE Act to temporarily halt all immigration, citing the highest number of foreign-born residents in US history. He slams the Senate for stalling the Save America Act, advocating for immediate legislative action to reform the immigration system amidst rising concerns about foreign nationals.

A "ringleader" has been sentenced and several other suspects charged in Illinois in connection with a widespread conspiracy to defraud the federal immigration system by helping noncitizens seek visa protections reserved for crime victims who assist law enforcement.

Parth Nayi of Illinois was sentenced Thursday to two years in federal prison for participating in hundreds of staged armed robberies at small businesses and eateries in and around Chicago and helping "coach" the supposed " victims" through plans to apply for U visas in exchange for cash.

"[Nayi] was the main organizer and at the center of almost every single one of the hundreds of staged robberies that were perpetrated. [The] defendant significantly corrupted the federal U-Visa program, designed to provide a benefit to a particularly vulnerable group—foreign nationals who are victims of serious crimes while visiting the United States," Assistant U.S. Attorney Saqib Mohammad Hussain wrote in the case’s sentencing memo.
TRUMP ADMIN’S FRAUD CRACKDOWN TARGETS FOREIGNERS ACCUSED OF INFILTRATING US FEDERAL PROGRAMS
A person holds a citizenship application from USCIS. (David Paul Morris/Getty Images)
Thousands of people posing as crime victims paid Nayi to participate in the scheme, prosecutors said.

Alleged co-conspirators Bhikhabhai Patel, Nilesh Patel, Ravinaben Patel and Rajnikumar Patel reached out to Nayi to pose as victims of the staged robberies so they could apply for U visas, which were created under a 2000 law meant to protect trafficking victims and "battered immigrant women."
Rep. Christopher Smith, R-N.J., lead sponsor of the anti-trafficking legislation that created the U visa, expressed outrage over the alleged abuse of the program.

"Anyone who engages in visa fraud or falsifies claims to obtain any government benefit should be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law, and if guilty, jailed," Smith told Fox News Digital on Tuesday.

"It is especially egregious to abuse a program designed to help victims of human trafficking — often women and children — who are cooperating with police and are working to recover from their extraordinary trauma. We must hold abusive criminals accountable."
Prosecutors said Nayi and another suspect, Kewon Young, recruited people to serve as armed "robbers" who at times "struck purported victims to make the staged robbery appear real."
Nayi and alleged co-conspirator Kewon Young organized and participated in staged robberies of shops and bodegas.

After the "robberies," the purported victims would be coached to submit I-918 supplements to law enforcement so authorities could certify that they had been victims of a violent crime and could seek U visas.
An I-918 form would then be submitted to U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) seeking protected legal status in the United States.

Purported victims paid Nayi as much as $30,000 to take part in the staged robberies, prosecutors said. During one robbery, a store employee was critically injured by a gunshot fired by one of the alleged assailants.
ICE ARRESTS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ILLINOIS TEACHER LINKED TO TREN DE ARAGUA MASS SHOOTING
Indian nationals charged visa fraud scheme involving fake robberies at Massachusetts stores. Federal authorities say 11 defendants staged armed robberies to claim U visa benefits. (FBI Boston/X)

During a July 2023 "robbery" at a Chicago liquor store, one of the alleged assailants accidentally discharged his weapon and "critically" injured an employee, according to CWB Chicago. The perpetrators then fled in a stolen vehicle, according to the outlet.
Fox News Digital reached out to Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson and Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker for comment.

Johnson has repeatedly lambasted federal immigration enforcement, particularly under the Trump administration, likening its actions to an America that appears as if the "Confederacy won" the Civil War.
Bhikhabhai Patel allegedly posed as a victim at a Chicago Dunkin' in 2023 before filing a fraudulent U visa application.
Ravinaben Patel allegedly posed as a victim at a second Dunkin' and filed a false police report about the incident.
The 2024 indictment identified more than a dozen locations used in the scheme, including businesses outside Illinois, such as a Subway in Louisiana and a truck stop in Middle Tennessee.

The DOJ’s indictment indicates five others besides Nayi have been convicted but does not specify their names.

Fox News Digital reached out to USCIS, DHS and ICE for comment.
Born and raised in Allentown, Pennsylvania, worked in both the New York and Washington bureaus for Fox News since 2013.

title: House report says NYC prosecutors tailored plea deals to shield illegal immigrants from deportation
summary: House Judiciary Committee claims New York City district attorneys trained prosecutors to craft immigration-safe plea deals for noncitizen defendants.
story: ICE New York City Field Office Director Ken Genalo reveals the criminal histories of the suspects charged in the stabbing of an NYPD detective. Genalo discusses Dominican Republic nationals D'Angelo Rafael Jean Caraballo, Sneider Mejia Bautista, and Eduardo Paulino, highlighting their prior arrests and immigration status. Genalo calls for cooperation between local law enforcement and federal immigration authorities to protect communities.

New York City prosecutors from all five boroughs have given "preferential treatment" to noncitizens who commit crimes, all to help them avoid deportation, according to a report from the GOP-led House Judiciary Committee.

The committee, chaired by Rep. Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, said nonpublic documents obtained through its oversight work revealed new details about the extent to which the city's district attorney's offices sought to limit the immigration consequences of criminal prosecutions.

Some of the report's most serious allegations came against Bronx District Attorney Darcel Clark. The report claims she "trains prosecutors in her office to conceal certain facts" from defendants' conviction records and pursue charges that would not trigger deportation.

Internal materials from the Bronx DA's office explicitly instruct prosecutors to leave references to firearms out of conviction records to maintain "immigration-conscious plea bargaining," according to the report.
Bronx County District Attorney Darcel Clark attends the 54th Annual Bronx Ball at Bally's Golf Links at Ferry Point on May 16, 2026 in Bronx, New York. (Joy Malone/Getty Images)
SOROS-BACKED DA ACCUSED OF GOING EASY ON ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS GETS SQUEEZED BY HOUSE GOP

In cases of domestic violence or crimes against children — offenses that are often deportable under the Immigration and Nationality Act — Bronx prosecutors were told to leave out defendants' relationships with their alleged victims and pursue charges that did not specify the ages of child victims.
Clark, who has been the Bronx DA since 2016, was also accused of encouraging prosecutors to charge foreign nationals with "nonexistent, legally impossible" crimes to skirt deportation.

The report's authors offered the example of Clark's staff getting someone to plead guilty to "attempted reckless assault," a crime they described as legally impossible because someone cannot intend to act recklessly. A plea to such a crime, they said, could allow a noncitizen defendant to stay in the country indefinitely.

New York courts nevertheless allow defendants to plead guilty to such hypothetical offenses as part of negotiated plea deals. The Court of Appeals, the state's highest court, upheld the legal concept this year.
The New York State Court of Appeals building on Oct. 2, 2024, in Albany, New York. (Will Waldron/Albany Times Union via Getty Images)
DENVER, BOULDER IGNORED ICE DETAINERS FOR MIGRANTS WITH CHILD ABUSE, ASSAULT ARRESTS, HOUSE GOP REPORT REVEALS

The practice is not limited to the Bronx. State data obtained by the Immigrant Defense Project showed 289 convictions for attempted reckless assault across New York City from 2015 through 2025, including 50 in the Bronx.
The House Judiciary Committee also pointed to similar practices within the Queens DA's office, led by Melinda Katz since 2020.

It cited a May 2026 email from a Queens prosecutor informing an NYPD detective that the DA's office had "basically made a [plea] deal which is ‘immigration safe’ while still having [the defendant] plea to multiple crimes and do some jail time."

Queens prosecutors were also instructed to "exercise extreme caution" when resolving cases involving noncitizens and to consult the office's immigration specialist when considering plea deals for them, the report said.
Queens District Attorney Melinda Katz is pictured during the arraignment of Roman Amatitla in Queens, New York, on April 9, 2026. (Theodore Parisienne / New York Daily News via Getty Images)
WATCH: DEM DEMANDS 'ONE CASE' WHERE SANCTUARY CITIES DIDN'T TURN OVER ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS; DHS PROVIDES LIST

Over in the Manhattan office, the report said DA Alvin Bragg issued a memo in 2022 telling prosecutors to "seek dispositions that avoid immigration consequences for all misdemeanors, and all felonies" where prosecutors generally did not expect defendants to receive jail time.
Bragg's office responded to the committee by describing its January 2022 policy as "outdated," adding that it had updated it to give prosecutors discretion on individual cases.
The DA's offices in Brooklyn and Staten Island were alleged to have used comparable tactics when dealing with noncitizen defendants, according to the report.
In a statement to Fox News Digital, the Staten Island DA's office called the House Judiciary Committee's report "flagrantly false and patently political."

"[The Richmond County District Attorney's Office] has and will continue to ask ICE to let us prosecute and convict criminals before they deport them because Congress has failed to secure our borders. That is the only way to guarantee our victims justice and to keep our communities safe. If you believe in law and order, that’s the only way to do the job," the office said.

Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg speaks at a press conference as he comments on the outcome in the retrial of former film producer Harvey Weinstein on June 12, 2025 in New York City. (Yuki Iwamura-Pool/Getty Images)
DHS SECRETARY BASHES NEW YORK LEADERSHIP AFTER ANNOUNCING THOUSANDS OF ARRESTS IN SWEEPING OPERATION
The four other offices referenced in the report did not immediately respond to a Fox News Digital request for comment. The mayor's office also did not immediately respond.

Citywide sanctuary policies led the NYPD to decline 20,255 immigration detainers between July 2018 and June 2026, the report said. Detainers are federal requests asking local authorities to hold certain noncitizens briefly so Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) can take them into custody.
The city's Department of Correction also declined all 2,852 ICE detainers it received during the same period, according to the report.
These figures are not necessarily surprising, given that each mayoral administration throughout that period has limited city agencies from cooperating with ICE.

Federal agents walk near the scene where a man was shot by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer during an operation in the Bronx borough of New York City on Oct. 8, 2026. (Charly Triballeau / AFP via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

What stands out, however, is that nearly half of those detainers — almost 10,000 — were lodged between July 2025 and June 2026, an indicator that the second Trump administration has acted far more aggressively in its attempts to scoop up noncitizens arrested by local police than either the Biden administration or the first Trump administration.
The House Judiciary Committee's findings come as House Republicans push legislation that would prevent state and local governments from restricting cooperation with federal immigration authorities.
In March, the committee advanced the Shut Down Sanctuary Policies Act — a bill that has stalled in the House — and the report said lawmakers would continue investigating sanctuary jurisdictions.
James Cirrone is a writer on the Breaking/Trending News team at Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to james.cirrone@fox.com.

title: Armed state Senate hopeful triggers police manhunt near grade school as alarming tweets go viral
summary: Jonathan Miller posted cryptic messages on X during an armed standoff with Cary police near Resurrection Lutheran School on Monday morning..
story: A panel of independent voters Doug Boyer, Rick Gagliano and Eric Mitchell discuss their top priorities and the key issues impacting their midterm votes on 'Fox & Friends First.'
This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

Police arrested a Libertarian North Carolina state Senate candidate Monday after an hours-long armed standoff near a private school, ending a tense confrontation that unfolded as the candidate posted threatening messages on social media.

Jonathan Miller, a Libertarian challenging a Democratic incumbent for a North Carolina state Senate seat, raised widespread concern Monday when he began making cryptic and viral posts on X suggesting that he was in the process of an armed pursuit with law enforcement.

"The whole police department is chasing me with guns drawn. This should be fun," he wrote around 9:38 a.m. "I've got six shots and the high ground. I hope they don't find me, but if they do it's going to be a hell of a show."
LIBERTARIAN TECH MOGUL TO HIT DSA WITH AN EIGHT-FIGURE SPENDING NUKE
Police stand armed outside Jonathan D. Miller’s apartment; Miller's mugshot  (WRAL; Cary Police Department)

A number of individuals pleaded with Miller to lay down his arms and surrender, including 2024 Libertarian presidential nominee Chase Oliver. Responding to Oliver at 10:04 a.m., Miller claimed that he had "reached the tree line," indicating that he was attempting to hide in the woods.
Responding to another user offering to send him money, Miller claimed that he "gave away all [his] money to charity" and that he didn’t "want or need yours."

Police said they received calls from concerned members of the public after Miller posted messages Sunday night suggesting he was considering suicide. Officers attempted to check on his welfare Monday morning, and during a subsequent encounter, Miller was carrying a firearm. Police said he fled after being ordered not to touch the weapon.
'MODERATE' AG'S OFFICE TURNED TO GROUPS THAT SPENT YEARS SUING PRISONS FOR RECRUITING HELP, EMAILS REVEAL
A large law enforcement presence was reported at the scene. (WGMB)
WRAL, a local NBC affiliate, managed to get Miller on the phone during his standoff with the police, where he gave his side of the story.

"Last night I was pretty depressed and suicidal, and I sort of put a suicide note on X, and it has gone quite viral," he told WRAL during one such call. "Actually, millions of people have seen it. I usually get about 50 views on my post, but this one has gone super viral on me. I spent all night crying, and angry and upset, and depressed, and all the emotions. And this morning I was tired, but I had things I needed to do. And I didn't kill myself.

"So I got up and made coffee," Miller continued, "and I had two sips of coffee, and I went outside to have a cigarette, and while I was having a cigarette, a police officer approached me, knew my name, saw that I had a holstered revolver on my hip, so he drew his weapon and told me to keep my hands away from mine. I told him I was going to refuse that order, and I backed away slowly until I was far enough away from him to turn and run, and then I turned and ran into the woods."
DOJ OPENS NEW PATHWAY TO RESTORE FEDERAL GUN RIGHTS FOR CERTAIN BARRED INDIVIDUALS
The North Carolina state Capitol building in Raleigh. (Getty Images)
Cary Police Chief Terry Sult stated that Miller had a warrant for being a felon in possession of a firearm.

Police expressed fear that the public could be in harm's way as a result of the standoff, urging pedestrians and motorists to avoid the surrounding area. The armed confrontation unfolded near Resurrection Lutheran School, a private K-8 school that was placed under a code yellow lockdown for part of Monday as police searched for Miller, according to local reports.

"They had some hostage negotiator type dude call me. While I was distracted talking with him on the phone they were moving in around me. Luckily I spotted one of them and took off," Miller posted to X around 1:46 p.m.

Around 3 p.m., law enforcement officers closed in on Miller and arrested him without incident. He has been charged with communicating threats, resisting a public officer, going armed to the terror of the people and possession of a firearm by a felon. No shots were fired during the confrontation, according to police.
The Libertarian Party of North Carolina told the New York Post that it was "aware of the situation," thanking law enforcement for "pursuing a solution without involving violence."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Miller is running for office on a relatively standard Libertarian platform of weakening legal protections for police, repealing drug laws and reducing economic regulations.

title: Schumer, Dems are quietly betting big on one sleeper race in the Deep South
summary: National Democrats reserved $1.2 million in Mississippi ads for Scott Colom as they target Cindy Hyde-Smith's Senate seat in a GOP stronghold.
story: With the midterm elections approaching, a Mississippi rally emphasizes the high stakes of the Senate race. President Trump championed Cindy Hyde-Smith for the United States Senate while accusing opponent Scott Colom of being a "shameless phony" funded by George Soros.
National Democrats are getting aggressive in the homestretch of this election cycle, sending money and party figureheads to a state that, for decades, has been out of reach.

Mississippi has been a Republican stronghold for the GOP in the Senate since the 1980s, but in a political environment that is proving tough for incumbents of the party in power, Democrats appear to smell blood in the water.
But Republicans aren’t buying the last-minute play in the Deep South, arguing that it’s a reach, at best, to make the race competitive.
DEMOCRATS SEE NEW CHANCES TO FLIP RED STATES — BUT A $400M GOP SPENDING ADVANTAGE COULD DERAIL THEIR PLANS
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer attends a press conference on China AI export controls at the U.S. Capitol on Sept. 23, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Getty Images)
"Largely, I think they’re just throwing s--- at the wall at this point," a GOP political operative told Fox News Digital.

The Senate Majority PAC, a political action committee with close ties to Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., reserved $1.2 million in advertising in the state to boost Scott Colom, a district attorney mounting a bid against Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith.

And major figures in the Democratic Party, like former Vice President Kamala Harris and former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, have also made the trip or are set to appear in the state — Buttigieg is scheduled to hold a rally on Mississippi’s Gulf Coast on Tuesday.
Jake Monssen, Hyde-Smith’s campaign manager, told Fox News Digital in a statement, "This is simply Washington insiders making a last-ditch effort to give life to Scott Colom's failing campaign."

"Scott is bankrolled by the radical left because he is in lockstep with their agenda," Monssen said. "He supports tax increases, open borders, taxpayer benefits for illegal immigrants, and sex change surgeries for minors."

Like in other races across the Senate map, Colom has a fight with history to contend with. Mississippi has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1982, and the Magnolia State has consistently supported President Donald Trump.
TRUMP-BACKED SENATOR ADMITS GOP FACES NIGHTMARE SCENARIO IN STATE REPUBLICANS HAVEN'T LOST IN 90 YEARS
But Colom believes that the ground operation he’s developed while national Democrats stayed away from the state is what would put him over the top against Hyde-Smith, not the last-minute support.
"It could be enough," Colom told Fox News Digital. "I mean, the thing is, the people of Mississippi built this campaign."
Colom went on the offensive against Hyde-Smith, arguing that she "refuses to debate, she doesn’t campaign."

"Because of that, I was able to build momentum on the ground, which means now that it's getting attention, now that it's getting resources, I'm able to take advantage of it in a way that other candidates couldn't," he said.

Republicans aren’t resting on their laurels in the state, however. The Senate Leadership Fund, a political action committee closely aligned with Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., teed up a seven-figure ad buy there in response to Democrats’ spending.
And Trump appeared in Corinth, Mississippi, on Monday to rally for Hyde-Smith. He made a similar pitch to voters that he’s done at every rally stop this midterm cycle: pretend he’s on the ballot.
"In this election, if you would, I'm asking you to pretend that I'm on the ballot," Trump said. "And the reason is that when I'm on the ballot, exactly 49% more people show up."

Jonathan Klingler, a professor of political science at the University of Mississippi, told Fox News Digital that the increased spending and national attention to a once-sleepy race have generated the "talking point of Mississippi as evidence for momentum and building a Democratic wave."
THUNE MAKES BOLD PREDICTION ABOUT REPUBLICANS' SENATE CHANCES AS GOP PULLS MILLIONS FROM KEY RACES
District Attorney Scott Colom, center, is running for Senate against Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, R-Miss., and has backers with deep pockets in the Soros family. (Courtesy of Colom Senate campaign)
"So at least I'm not — I can't say whether that's the intent of the funding here or visits, but that is the effect," he said.

There are also voter demographics that both Hyde-Smith and Colom have to contend with. Mississippi has the highest share of Black voters in the country at nearly 40% of the electorate. In order for Colom and "Democrats to be successful, they simply have to peel off a larger share of White voters," Klingler said.
There’s another storyline underneath the headlines of this race, too.
Hyde-Smith and Colom have a history dating back to the Biden administration, when the lawmaker blocked his nomination to serve as a district court judge in Mississippi.

"Instead of saving himself the embarrassment of being denied a job twice by Hyde-Smith, Colom is running a campaign backed by Chuck Schumer, funded by George Soros, and built on pro-transgender and other far-left policies," National Republican Senatorial Committee spokeswoman Bernadette Breslin told Fox News Digital.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

That’s not Colom’s motivating factor, however. He had just left Trump's northeast Mississippi rally where he spoke to voters about their main concerns, "everybody I talked to, gas prices, grocery prices," and tariffs, he said.
But Colom said his personal dispute with Hyde-Smith was not his primary motivation.

"I'll tell you, as a Christian, I forgive her for that. That's not a motivating factor for me," Colom said. "I mean, as a district attorney, I have to prosecute cases where people lost their loved ones to gun violence. So, you know, and I’ve seen them forgive that person."

"So that's not the motivating factor," he continued. "For me, it's really the betrayal of the America First movement, right? Like she was supposed to help President Trump get lower grocery prices. Well, she betrayed us. We're not getting lower grocery prices."
Alex Miller is a writer for Fox News Digital covering the U.S. Senate.

title: Illinois man accused of threatening Congress with white substances in letters marked with his return address
summary: Matthew Unglesbee allegedly told the FBI the white powder substance was salt and that he mailed the threatening letters to Congress as a joke.
story: A letter sent to a congressperson in Illinois containing an unknown white substance (U.S. District Court in the Central District of Illinois)
An Illinois man was charged with two felonies Monday after allegedly sending letters containing an unknown white powder substance to members of Congress, according to a criminal complaint.

Matthew G. Unglesbee was charged with false information and hoaxes and mailing threatening communications after four members of Congress received the letters, which were marked with his return address, according to the complaint.
Unglesbee told the FBI the substance in the letters was salt and that he mailed them as a joke, the complaint read.
OHIO MAN CHARGED OVER GRAPHIC THREATS TO KILL TRUMP, BEHEAD GOP LAWMAKER

The FBI received a tip that Unglesbee had sent the letters on Oct. 16. The tipster had overheard Unglesbee at a restaurant saying he had mailed suspicious substances to members of Congress, the complaint stated.
The tipster allegedly provided authorities with Unglesbee’s full name, address and date of birth.
MAN INDICTED FOR ALLEGEDLY POSTING GRUESOME DEATH THREATS AGAINST KRISTI NOEM, PAM BONDI ON SOCIAL MEDIA

Members of the FBI’s field office in Chicago responded to the offices of three members of Congress in the northern Illinois area after receiving the tip and a 911 call from one of the congressional offices.
FBI Chicago field office. (AFP PHOTO/Stan HONDA via Getty Images)

"A staff member at Congressperson A's office, the first office to receive a letter, noticed that the letter felt like it contained a powder and the staffer could hear something inside the letter," the complaint read. This staff member called 911.
BIOWEAPON THREAT EXPOSED AS ANTHROPIC SOUNDS ALARM ON FOREIGN ACTORS PLOTTING VIRUS EXPERIMENTS
The office had already been on high alert, having received a similar letter within the previous few weeks, according to the complaint.
All three letters contained "a white granular substance" and a handwritten letter which read "HA HA," the complaint stated.
CONGRESS IS A HUGE TARGET FOR SPIES. MEMBERS AND STAFF NEED A WAKE-UP CALL AND TRAINING
The seal of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) on the J. Edgar Hoover Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) building in Washington, DC, on March 10, 2025   (BRENDAN SMIALOWSKI/AFP )

On Friday, FBI Chicago responded to the office of a fourth member of Congress, a senator in the Northern District of Illinois. The senator had also received an envelope with a white granular substance, also with a letter which also read, "HAH enjoy the gift."
All four letters were marked with Unglesbee’s name and return address, according to the complaint.
FAA EMPLOYEE CHARGED WITH ALLEGEDLY THREATENING TO KILL PRESIDENT TRUMP IN EMAIL TO WHITE HOUSE

FBI Task Force Officer Chris Hobbs, who wrote the criminal complaint, characterized the letters as a common intimidation tactic, pointing out that preliminary lab testing "did not detect the presence of chemical or biological toxins in the white granular substance."

The FBI interviewed Unglesbee at his home Saturday when he allegedly confessed to sending the letters, telling law enforcement that he heard someone in a restaurant talking about similar letters Congress members had received.
Unglesbee confessed to the FBI that he used salt because it looked like anthrax. (Ronaldo Bolaños/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)
UTAH MAN CHARGED WITH ATTEMPTED HATE CRIME AFTER ALLEGED THREAT TO 'BLOW UP' SYNAGOGUE
He told the FBI he knew his powder would be perceived as potentially being anthrax and anticipated people responding with hazmat suits.
He also told the FBI that the powder was salt, claiming he used salt specifically because it looked like anthrax.
PENNSYLVANIA MAN ACCUSED OF PLOTTING ISIS ATTACK ARRESTED WITH RIFLE AND 190 ROUNDS OF AMMUNITION: DOJ
"Unglesbee claimed he was joking but recognized that the recipients would not know he was joking and could perceive it as a threat," the complaint read.
The FBI searched Unglesbee's home and found a fifth letter marked with one of the congresspeople's Washington, D.C., office's address.
The FBI also determined that Unglesbee sent the letters on Oct. 19.

Fox News Digital contacted the FBI for further information.

title: Kamala Harris calls Trump administration 'most callous and corrupt' in American history
summary: Kamala Harris called the Trump White House the "most callous and corrupt" administration in history while campaigning for David Crowley in Wisconsin.
story: While stumping for Wisconsin's Democratic gubernatorial nominee David Crowley, former Vice President Kamala Harris cast the Trump administration as a brutal government that is threatening key democratic norms.

While on the campaign trail Monday for Democrats ahead of the midterms, former Vice President Kamala Harris offered some of her harshest criticism of the Trump White House yet, calling it the "most callous and corrupt and incompetent" presidential administration in American history.

Twice during her speech at an event for David Crowley, the Democratic nominee for governor in Wisconsin, Harris accused the Trump administration of wielding an agenda of "brutality" against Americans.
Though in her lambasting of President Donald Trump's character and leadership style, she didn't mention him by name once.

"We in this room, I know, understand that the measure of the strength of the leader is based on who you lift up, not who you beat down," Harris said. "Unlike some other people who are constantly looking in the mirror, David is looking at the people. That's the kind of leader we want."

Former Vice President Kamala Harris speaks during a Women for Crowley campaign event hosted by Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial candidate David Crowley at the Pfister Hotel on Oct. 26, 2026, in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Scott Olson/Getty Images)
KAMALA HARRIS CLAIMS GOP 'CHEATING' AHEAD OF MIDTERMS, SAYS SHE'S FOCUSED ON STOPPING THE 'MADNESS'
Her more specific, policy-based attacks came against Rep. Tom Tiffany, R-Wis., Crowley's opponent in the gubernatorial race.

Harris noted that Tiffany supported Trump's efforts to overturn the 2020 election based on unsubstantiated claims of widespread fraud, before framing the upcoming election as a test of longstanding democratic norms.
"Let's talk about the fact that David's opponent denied the election of 2020. By the way, we won. Yes, you can call me former madam Vice President. We won that election," Harris said.

She continued: "We are now in the phase of the moment in our democracy, while we can still hold on to it, where the people's voice reigns, where the will of the people reigns, where the power of the people is demonstrated by what we do to organize."
Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate David Crowley snaps a selfie with his wife Ericka and former Vice President Kamala Harris during a campaign event on Oct. 26, 2026. (Scott Olson/Getty Images)
MAPPED: THE STATES TRUMP AND TOP DEMOCRATS ARE TARGETING BEFORE ELECTION DAY
At an earlier event on Monday, Crowley called Harris a "huge mentor" of his, adding that his wife loves her.

Tiffany pounced on the connection in a social media post, accusing Crowley of sharing Harris' support for higher taxes, "taxpayer benefits for illegals" and "Green New Deal policies" that he argued would drive up energy costs.

Over the last several weeks, Harris has barnstormed through several key presidential battlegrounds to campaign alongside Democrats, including Nevada gubernatorial candidate Aaron Ford and Senate candidates Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan and Chris Pappas in New Hampshire.

Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and former Vice President Kamala Harris participate in a roundtable discussion about reproductive health at Birth Detroit on Sept. 22, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (David Guralnick - Pool/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Her increased involvement has only fueled speculation that she is laying the groundwork for another White House run in 2028.
During a September event with NAACP leaders in Detroit, Harris said she has yet to decide whether she'll run for president again.
"I do sincerely believe '28 won't matter if we don't get through '26," she said.
James Cirrone is a writer on the Breaking/Trending News team at Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to james.cirrone@fox.com.

title: FBI raids Beverly Hills mansion as part of Eric Swalwell investigation
summary: The FBI raided a Beverly Hills mansion tied to Eric Swalwell as the former congressman faces sexual misconduct accusations from at least five women.
story: Federal authorities raided a California mansion related to an investigation into former Rep. Eric Swalwell, D-Calif., on Tuesday morning.
BEVERLY HILLS – Federal authorities raided a California mansion belonging to billionaire Stephen Cloobeck on Tuesday morning, Fox News has learned.

The FBI targeted Cloobeck's Beverly Hills mansion in connection with an investigation into disgraced former Rep. Eric Swalwell, D-Calif. Swalwell resigned from Congress and withdrew from the California gubernatorial race earlier this year after facing multiple accusations of sexual misconduct.

Law enforcement executed the raid at roughly 6 a.m. local time with at least two dozen agents participating. Authorities searched the massive property for several hours but offered no details about what they found.
Several people were taken out of the house in handcuffs, but they were all released soon after. Cloobeck was not at the residence at the time of the raid.
FBI SEIZES SWALWELL’S DEVICES AT AIRPORT AS SEXUAL MISCONDUCT INVESTIGATION ESCALATES: SOURCES
Rep. Eric Swalwell (D-Calif.) speaks during a House Judiciary Committee hearing with FBI Director Kash Patel in the Rayburn House Office Building on Sept. 17, 2025. (Win McNamee/Getty Images)
The raid was linked to a sex worker reportedly connected to the investigation.
Cloobeck is a longtime supporter of Swalwell's political campaigns.

In August, the FBI searched Swalwell's D.C. home and seized his electronic devices at San Francisco International Airport during an operation. The operation was related to a probe into sexual misconduct, according to sources familiar with the incident. He was not arrested or detained.
Cloobeck was arrested earlier this year in an unrelated case, in which he faced charges of attempting to influence witnesses in a criminal case against his fiancée.
At least five women, including one former staffer, have accused Swalwell of sexual misconduct or rape.

Swalwell told FBI agents he had "physical relations" with Fang on a handful of occasions, according to declassified FBI records released Monday by the White House.
Their last sexual encounter occurred in March 2015, according to Swalwell’s account in the FBI records.
The documents were released by the White House's new Government Transparency Task Force.
Swalwell was interviewed by the FBI first in May 2015 and later in March 2016 regarding his relationship with Fang.
Fang had suspected ties to China’s Ministry of State Security (MSS), and her parents were reportedly considered known Chinese intelligence officers.
SWALWELL CALLS SEXUAL MISCONDUCT ALLEGATIONS 'FLAT OUT FALSE,' SAYS HE WILL FIGHT THEM 'WITH EVERYTHING'

Lonna Drewes, a woman with sexual misconduct allegations against U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell, reacts as she holds a press conference with her attorneys Lisa Bloom and Arick Fudali in Beverly Hills, California, on April 14, 2026. (Jill Connelly/Reuters)

title: Fox News Power Rankings: As Iran looms large, can the GOP keep the faithful?
summary: Trump's approval dropped to 36% amid the war in Iran, reshaping the 2026 midterms, but the Senate map through deep-red states keeps GOP alive.
story: Fox News' Bill Hemmer examines the latest Power Rankings with five Senate races in toss-up territory, as President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance campaign in key states one week before the midterm elections.
It seems like there are two electorates in these midterms.
The first is frustrated with President Donald Trump and ready to reject Republicans. It includes growing numbers of independent, rural and Hispanic voters who say they’ll vote for a Democrat.
That’s what the latest round of House polling shows, including a survey last week that had Democrats up 11 points on the generic ballot, and Fox’s most recent national poll.
SCHOEN, COOPERMAN: DEMOCRATS COULD BE RIDING A MIDTERM WAVE. THESE NUMBERS SHOULD TERRIFY THE GOP
Fox News Power Rankings House forecast. (Remy Numa/Fox News)

The second electorate is wavering on Republicans but won’t necessarily hand Democrats the Senate. These are the voters in the Midwest and a few other places. They say they prefer the Democrat or Republican in their states by a point or two at most.
That’s the right conclusion from most of the battleground Senate polling.
How could both things be true? In other words, if Democrats have such a wide lead in the House, won’t the Senate fall too?

Both are true, and a big lead in the House doesn’t necessarily translate to the Senate. These voters are all in the same electorate, and they only seem divorced from each other because the House and Senate maps are so far apart this year.
DEMOCRATS THINK A BLUE WAVE IS BUILDING. HERE ARE 3 FORCES THAT COULD STOP IT
Fox News Power Rankings Senate forecast. (Remy Numa/Fox News)
The president’s declining approval rating and Democratic advantages on the issues will likely deliver them the House and possibly by many seats.
Those advantages have also allowed the blue team to play in a lot of Senate races that Republicans thought were unreachable, but only to the point of making them battlegrounds.

The road to a Senate majority goes through several states that Trump won by 11 points or more. Democrats can win any of these races. If Republicans turn out and stay loyal to their party, the climb for the left will be steep.
That’s why the Senate is a toss-up. Voters could give Democrats a majority and maybe with several seats to spare. They could also let the Republicans keep control.
We’ll find out in seven days.
Democrats have strong advantages on most key issues

In his 11-year political career, President Trump has triumphed over almost all the threats to his power. The exception was the coronavirus pandemic, which was the top issue for voters in the 2020 election and ushered in the Biden presidency.
It was also one of the few threats that Trump has faced from abroad.

This time, Trump and the Republicans face a new foreign opponent: Iran. The administration’s decision to start joint U.S.-Israeli military strikes against the nation in February has cast a shadow over the GOP.
VOTERS PREPARE TO WEIGH-IN ON TRUMP'S ECONOMY AS COSTS CONTINUE TO SURGE
Fox News Power Rankings on approval of President Donald Trump. (Remy Numa/Fox News)

First, it has impacted Trump’s approval rating, which will decide the fate of many congressional Republicans and has fallen since the war began. It was 44% in the last pre-war survey and sits at 36% now.
NOT EVEN SKY HIGH GAS PRICES OR THE IRAN WAR WILL STOP TRUMP SUPPORTERS VOTING MAGA
Fox News Power Rankings on the top issues on the ballot. (Remy Numa/Fox News)

The war has also given Democrats advantages on the top issues. In Fox’s October survey, Iran played a role in four issues that more than two-thirds of voters said they were concerned about: inflation (85%), gas prices (83%), government leadership (79%) and the war in Iran itself (75%).
Fox News Power Rankings on top issues on the ballot. (Remy Numa/Fox News)
Most voters said they preferred the Democrats to handle those issues: 16 points on inflation, 12 points on gas prices, 11 points on leadership and 9 points on foreign policy.
Republicans are competitive on home turf
Still, voters are not convinced that the Senate should change hands.
That comes down to the territory. Trump won seven of these 10 battleground states in 2024 and six of them by double digits. That includes Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, South Carolina and Texas.
Fox News Power Rankings on battleground states. (Remy Numa/Fox News)
Democrats don’t need to win all of those states to take the Senate, but it’s hard to see how they get to 51 seats without at least two of them.
While former Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown leads in Ohio, the other states are close. Turnout, a polling error in either direction or both could decide them.

There are also a lot of undecided votes. In Alaska, Iowa and Kansas, three states with recent high-quality polling, an average of 10% of voters say they haven’t decided who they will support or won’t support the major candidates.
Fox News Power Rankings on red states. (Remy Numa/Fox News)

Any guess on how those voters will break at the ballot box is only a guess. All we know from prior results is that the overall electorate leans conservative, so the Democrats have the tougher assignment to bring them over to their side (or keep them at home).
There are far fewer undecided voters in Texas, where last week’s Fox News Poll showed a tied race at 49%-49%.

If Democrats only win two Trump-won battlegrounds, they’ll need to win three other races where former Vice President Harris delivered single-digit victories in 2024: Maine, Minnesota and New Hampshire.

Democrats are ahead in the latter two. Maine could go either way. While Democrats win its presidential races, it could just as easily be considered a Republican state when Susan Collins is on the ballot.
The final Fox News Power Rankings for 2026 feature three shifts in the Senate and 19 in the House. A tight gubernatorial race is also on the move.
Senate: Democrats are favored in 48 seats as Ohio moves to Lean D
Fox News Power Rankings on Senate forecast. (Remy Numa/Fox News)

Both parties are three seats short of a majority in this forecast. Democrats are favored in 48 seats and Republicans are ahead in 47 (they would control the Senate with 50 seats because the vice president breaks ties).
Fox News Power Rankings on Senate forecast. (Remy Numa/Fox News)

On a good night for Democrats, the party would win most or all the toss-ups, taking their majority up to 53 seats. In that scenario, other competitive states would also come into focus, including two rated Lean R, and on a great Democratic night, two more rated Likely R.

A good night for the Republicans would see them simply hold on to most of the states they already have, up to a ceiling of 52 seats. The party also has opportunities to flip a couple of states, including Minnesota and New Hampshire.
Three states are moving in this forecast.
In Ohio, Brown has enjoyed a lead in three Fox News polls this year, including last week’s survey, which had him five points ahead of Republican incumbent Sen. Jon Husted at 52%-47%.
Fox News Power Rankings on Senate forecast. (Remy Numa/Fox News)

Ohio voters are very familiar with Brown, having sent him to the Senate three times. That has made it hard for Husted to campaign on socialism and woke politics, themes that Republicans elsewhere see as their strongest cards to play.
Ohio moves from Toss-up to Lean D.
("Lean D" means the Democrat has an edge but it’s still a highly competitive race. We define every ranking and the process for setting them on FoxNews.com.)
South Carolina’s Senate race is effectively open this year. Senator Darline Graham won her primary, but it was close: 52%-48%, and only after Trump rallied with her.
Fox News Power Rankings on Senate forecast. (Remy Numa/Fox News)
Graham has never faced a general electorate before, and she is about to do that in a poor issues environment both for her and the GOP.
Republicans view this as an uncomfortably close race.
South Carolina moves from Likely R to Lean R.
Mississippi is a Republican stronghold, but Trump’s decision to rally there over other deep red states is a sign that the party thinks it’s competitive.
GOP Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith faces Democratic District Attorney Scott Colom in a race where protein choice has become a breakout issue.
Fox News Power Rankings on Senate forecast. (Remy Numa/Fox News)
Mississippi moves from Solid R to Likely R.
House: The floor for Democrats ticks up four seats to 223
Democrats are still likely to flip the House this November, and in this forecast, they’re predicted to take at least 223 seats.
Fox News Power Rankings on House forecast. (Remy Numa/Fox News)
Since a good night for the Democrats would see them take most of the toss-up races, they could end up with as many as 240 seats.
Fox News Power Rankings on House forecast. (Remy Numa/Fox News)
(On a great Democratic night, the party would pick up most of the Lean R districts as well, taking them as high as 252 seats.)

Republicans have 195 seats in their columns. A good night for them would take that total up to around 212. That’s six short of a majority, but enough to make life difficult for the next Democratic House Speaker, who would have to balance the demands of the moderate and far-left wings of the party.
Fox News Power Rankings on House forecast. (Remy Numa/Fox News)

Nineteen more races have shifted in the Democrats’ direction this week, all on the same themes outlined in the last House update: national and district polling, top-of-the-ticket strength and rural voter erosion.

The earliest-closing districts on election night will give some sense of the House’s future. Keep an eye on Kentucky’s 6th district, which covers Lexington and a large central area of the state. Trump won here by 15 points in the last presidential election. Thanks to a combination of left-leaning college voters and farmers grappling with higher costs, it looks close this cycle. The district moves from Lean R to Toss-up.
Fox News Power Rankings on House forecast. (Remy Numa/Fox News)
Governor: Ad or no ad, the Ohio governor’s race moves to Lean D

Finally, Ohio’s gubernatorial race is also on the move. The campaign between Democrat Amy Acton and Republican Vivek Ramaswamy was the top story in politics last week after Ramaswamy ran an ad featuring Acton’s mother, who called her daughter a liar.
Fox News Power Rankings on the gubernatorial forecast. (Remy Numa/Fox News)

Acton has been estranged from her mother since age 12, when she says she and her brother left her family home because her mother’s husband was sexually abusing her. Acton’s brother now appears in a response ad discussing their family history.
Fox News Power Rankings on the gubernatorial forecast. (Remy Numa/Fox News)

This ratings change is less about the response to the ad (Ramaswamy and President Trump are supportive of the commercial; most others including Husted and Governor Mike DeWine are against it) than it is about the fact that the Ramaswamy campaign felt the need to run it.
While Ramaswamy sat only two points behind Acton in last week’s Fox poll, he’s an average of seven points behind in other high-quality polls since September.
Fox News Power Rankings on the gubernatorial forecast. (Remy Numa/Fox News)
The businessman and onetime presidential hopeful has struggled in favorability ratings throughout his political career. This ad is unlikely to help.
The Ohio governor’s race moves from Toss-up to Lean D.
