Why blocking political text messages doesn't work

You would think blocking a phone number would send a pretty clear message. Apparently, political texting operations don't always take the hint. I asked George why texts from the same political groups kept showing up after I blocked their numbers. "Well, you block one number, and you've only blocked one number," Weiner explained.

He introduced me to a technique called snowshoeing, which allows an organization to spread its messages across multiple phone numbers. A single campaign or political action committee (PAC) may use many different numbers to reach the same people. So, even after you block one sender, another number can deliver the next fundraising appeal.

For George, this frustration became personal. As a father of three, he worries about missing an important call from his children's school. "That could be the school, right? That could be an emergency," he explained. Instead, his phone often interrupts him with another fundraising appeal. He tried replying STOP, reporting messages and registering for the National Do Not Call Registry. Yet the interruptions continued. "I have done it all, and I still get these messages," Weiner said. That raises a question I've been asking for years. How did these organizations get our phone numbers in the first place?
How political campaigns get your phone number

You might assume a campaign needs your permission before adding your number to its texting list. Unfortunately, political outreach operates under rules that leave plenty of room for unsolicited messages. Weiner explained how phone numbers can circulate through political donor and voter databases. Campaigns may also combine registration information with commercially available data to identify potential supporters. Furthermore, organizations can purchase or exchange contact lists, allowing your information to reach groups you've never heard of.

Voter registration records vary by state, and phone numbers aren't necessarily public in those records. However, organizations can match voter information with other databases to build detailed contact profiles. Political donations can create additional exposure. As we've previously reported, federal political contribution records can reveal personal information, including your name and address, when disclosure requirements apply. Once your number enters this fundraising network, tracking every organization that holds it becomes extremely difficult.
The money behind nonstop political fundraising texts

Here's something from my conversation with George that really caught my attention. There's a substantial amount of money flowing through the political texting business, and the people sending these messages have financial reasons to keep doing it. Weiner pointed to approximately $65 million spent on political texting services during the 2024 election cycle, based on his analysis of Federal Election Commission records. He also believes 2026 spending could exceed that amount, although a final election-cycle total isn't yet available.

George also highlighted how much money individual political messaging vendors receive. According to PACspam's analysis of FEC records covering December 2008 through May 2026, reported payments totaled $17 million for Switchboard, $14.4 million for Mothership Strategies and $10.6 million for Message Digital. These figures span multiple election cycles and reflect reported payments to political messaging vendors, which may include services beyond texting.
Why political fundraising texts keep coming

"There is money to be made," Weiner told me. He explained that fundraising operations can keep paying to send messages as long as the donations they generate justify the expense. Even a small percentage of people responding with money can make another round of texts financially worthwhile. Some appeals claim a donation deadline is approaching or suggest a candidate faces an immediate financial emergency. Others use provocative headlines designed to make you react before thinking.

Weiner also raised concerns about how much money some PACs actually direct toward candidates. He pointed to investigations suggesting that certain organizations spend heavily on fundraising while relatively little reaches the candidate being promoted. PACs operate under different rules, however, and not all are established to make direct candidate contributions. That's why it's important to investigate where your donation will go. And this problem crosses political lines. Weiner stressed that organizations associated with different political parties use these tactics. The repeated pleas for money, he believes, can end up alienating the very voters campaigns want to reach. That brings us to an interesting way to investigate who's behind the messages.
How PACspam helps identify who's sending political texts

George created PACspam.org to give people more information about the organizations filling their phones with unsolicited political messages. "Our phones don't have to live like this," Weiner said while explaining why he built the tool. The free service analyzes political fundraising texts and attempts to identify the committee behind them. It can examine fundraising links and use public campaign finance information to help trace the organization responsible. PACspam also helps document complaints and tracks repeat offenders using information connected to FEC-registered committees. Its public leaderboard focuses on texting behavior rather than political affiliation. Meanwhile, its FEC Texting-Spend Explorer lets visitors investigate campaign spending on texting services. In some cases, PACspam can also help identify the texting technology provider that delivered the message. That last part is particularly interesting because those technology companies may serve multiple political organizations.

Rather than contacting only the committee asking for money, Weiner suggests contacting the texting platform when it can be identified. "They do answer," Weiner told me when I asked whether these companies respond to complaints. He described receiving a response from the legal department of a texting provider. That company explained how he could request placement on its own do-not-contact list. The approach could be more useful than blocking one phone number because it targets a provider that may handle messages for multiple political organizations. Still, one company's removal list won't necessarily apply to competing platforms. Of course, results can vary. An organization may use another platform, and some messages don't contain enough information to identify the sender. Still, contacting a texting provider offers another avenue to pursue.
DEM FUNDRAISING GIANT ACTBLUE ACCUSED OF FRAUDULENT DONATION 'COVER-UP' IN EXPLOSIVE REPORT
According to PACspam's analysis of FEC records, political messaging vendors received millions in reported payments between December 2008 and May 2026. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)
How to use PACspam.org
Getting started requires only a political text you've received. Here's what to do.

Visit PACspam.org.Copy the unwanted political message from your phone. You can also upload a screenshot if you prefer.Review the message or screenshot for personal details you don't want to share.Paste the message into the site's lookup tool, or upload your screenshot.Select Look up sender to analyze the message.Review any identified committee, fundraising link or texting provider.Use the generated complaint information to contact the relevant organization through available official channels. You can also review the site's reporting options.
Visit PACspam.org.
Copy the unwanted political message from your phone. You can also upload a screenshot if you prefer.
Review the message or screenshot for personal details you don't want to share.
Paste the message into the site's lookup tool, or upload your screenshot.
Select Look up sender to analyze the message.
Review any identified committee, fundraising link or texting provider.
Use the generated complaint information to contact the relevant organization through available official channels. You can also review the site's reporting options.

PACspam can prepare complaint information and help document unwanted political messages, but it doesn't automatically send those complaints on your behalf. It also cannot guarantee that your number will disappear from political texting lists. I also asked George an important privacy question. What happens to the information people submit? "We're not collecting your number. I just want that message," he said. According to Weiner, you don't need an account to use PACspam. Whole Whale also says uploaded screenshots are processed and discarded, while personal messages aren't displayed publicly. Those are the service's stated privacy practices, so I still recommend removing identifying details before submitting anything.
Are unsolicited political text messages legal?

Here's where things get frustrating. The Federal Communications Commission treats political texts differently depending on how they're sent. Political messages sent through an automatic telephone dialing system generally require prior express consent before reaching your cellphone. However, messages sent manually through peer-to-peer texting systems can fall outside those restrictions. That helps explain why so many campaign texts can reach people who never specifically requested them.

The National Do Not Call Registry generally doesn't cover political outreach either. So, registering your number may reduce some telemarketing calls without stopping political fundraising appeals. The FCC also says political campaigns should honor opt-out requests when recipients reply STOP. For robotexts covered by federal consent rules, revocation requests must generally be honored within 10 business days. However, an opt-out from one sender won't necessarily remove your number from other political organizations' databases.
5 ways to block political text messages and protect yourself
You may not be able to eliminate every political text, but several steps can reduce the interruptions and help protect your information.

If you receive a message from a legitimate political campaign or organization, replying STOP can unsubscribe you from that sender's messages. However, be selective. If the text looks suspicious or contains an unfamiliar fundraising link, avoid responding. Scammers sometimes impersonate political organizations, and engaging with suspicious messages may confirm that your number is active.
Your smartphone already has tools that can help move unwanted messages out of your main inbox. Here's where to find them.
On iPhone running iOS 27:
Open the Messages app.Tap the Filters button.Select Manage Filtering.Turn on Screen Unknown Senders.Make sure Filter Spam is enabled.
Open the Messages app.
Tap the Filters button.
Select Manage Filtering.
Turn on Screen Unknown Senders.
Make sure Filter Spam is enabled.

Unknown senders can move into a separate folder, reducing interruptions. If needed, tap Allow Notifications to choose which categories of unknown messages can still alert you. Availability varies by region.
On Google Pixel or Samsung Galaxy using Google Messages:
Open Google Messages.Tap your profile picture or icon.Select Messages settings.Tap Protection & safety.Select Spam protection.Turn on Enable spam protection, if available.
Open Google Messages.
Tap your profile picture or icon.
Select Messages settings.
Tap Protection & safety.
Select Spam protection.
Turn on Enable spam protection, if available.

Google Messages can flag suspicious texts and move some of them into the Spam & blocked folder. Menu options may vary by device and app version. Remember to review your filtered messages occasionally so important texts don't get overlooked.
FCC ROBOCALL CRACKDOWN COULD CHANGE PHONE PRIVACY
Unwanted political texts can interrupt your day, even after you've tried opting out or blocking previous senders. (Anna Barclay/Getty Images)
Blocking individual numbers can reduce messages from persistent senders, even though other numbers may still get through.

On an iPhone, open the unwanted conversation, tap the sender's icon, select Info and choose Block Contact. On an iPhone, reporting a message as spam doesn't automatically block the sender. You need to block the contact separately if you want messages from that number stopped.
On Google Messages, touch and hold the unwanted conversation, then tap Block. You can also select Report spam before confirming.
For additional guidance, see our guide to blocking phone numbers and texts.

You can forward unwanted political texts to 7726, which spells SPAM on a telephone keypad. This alerts your wireless carrier and can help its spam detection efforts. For suspected violations of federal calling or texting rules, you can also submit a complaint through the FCC Consumer Complaint Center. If the text appears to be a scam, report it to the Federal Trade Commission at reportfraud.ftc.gov/. Keep a screenshot of the suspicious message if you may need it for your report.

One of George's strongest recommendations involves political donations. If you want to support a candidate, find that candidate's official website yourself rather than following a link in an unsolicited text. During our interview, George warned that donating through unfamiliar political fundraising texts can encourage additional solicitations. He described how a successful donation might lead organizations to think, "We got one, let's send twice as many messages." His recommendation was straightforward: Give through the candidate's official website instead of an unsolicited fundraising link. That helps you verify who is receiving your money. However, even donating directly can lead to additional campaign messages, so review the site's privacy disclosures and contact preferences.

Additionally, consider limiting how widely your phone number appears online. Data brokers can collect and resell personal information, and removing your details from covered sites may reduce future exposure. Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com.

Keep in mind that commercial data removal services cannot erase legally required public campaign finance records. They also can't guarantee removal from every political organization's contact database.
Kurt's key takeaways

What struck me most about my conversation with George is how much money is being made from messages that so many of us desperately want to stop. We block numbers and ask to be removed, yet the texts keep coming. And the organizations making money from this system have little incentive to change it. I appreciate that George decided to do something about it. His PACspam tool offers a way to investigate who's behind these messages and push back through official complaint channels. I'd love to see political organizations become more accountable for how they use our personal information. After all, supporting a candidate shouldn't mean giving every fundraising operation unlimited access to your phone. Want to hear exactly how George is fighting back? Listen to my full interview with George Weiner on The CyberGuy Report podcast. We dig deeper into the political texting business, the companies behind it and what you can do when blocking numbers fails. And if you're ready to reduce even more unwanted messages, head to CyberGuyLive.com for my free Sick of Spam? class replay. You'll get practical advice for reducing robocalls, unwanted texts and junk email, along with a free spam-stopping checklist.

Should political campaigns have to get your permission before sending fundraising texts, and should the companies profiting from those messages face consequences when you repeatedly ask them to stop? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

title: Haitian national charged with murdering estranged wife outside Walmart after green card marriage goes awry
summary: Destino Jean Louis allegedly hid near a bush outside the Walmart where his estranged wife worked, waiting for her shift to end before the fatal shooting.
story: Fox News correspondent CB Cotton reports on a Haitian national being arrested and charged with first-degree murder of his estranged wife at a Walmart in Pennsylvania.

Haitian national Destino Jean Louis was charged with murder after he allegedly killed his wife outside a Pennsylvania Walmart store where she worked following the collapse of their marriage, according to court documents and a press release from the Montgomery County District Attorney's Office.

U.S. Marshals arrested Jean Louis on Friday morning in Philadelphia on charges related to overstaying his visa, which he had originally obtained through a now-terminated relief program for Haitian nationals. The district attorney's office then charged him in connection with the murder while he was in federal custody, authorities said.

"At 9 AM on Friday, October 23rd, Destino Jean Louis, 23, was arrested by [U.S. Marshals Service Philadelphia] on the 6600 block of N. 18th St for immigration violations. Louis, a Haitian national who overstayed his visa, was the prime suspect in the October 21st fatal shooting of a 45 year-old Walmart employee who had just left her shift," U.S. Marshals Service Philadelphia wrote in a Monday post on X.
ICE ARRESTS SOUTHWEST AIRLINES FLIGHT ATTENDANT IN NASHVILLE FOR ALLEGEDLY OVERSTAYING VISA SINCE 2021
U.S. Marshals take Destino Jean-Louis into custody. (U.S. Marshals Service Philadelphia)

Jean Louis' victim, identified by authorities as 45-year-old Latosha Ann Cooper, was his estranged wife whom he had married in March. Investigators told Fox29 that immigration officials had determined the marriage to be not legitimate and was only for immigration purposes.
AMERICAN WOMAN MASTERMINDS $6 MILLION MARRIAGE FRAUD SCHEME, DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE SAYS
In July, Cooper withdrew her petition to sponsor Jean Louis' visa, according to documents reviewed by Fox29.
U.S. Marshals arrest Destino Jean Louis in Philadelphia. (U.S. Marshals Service Philadelphia)

Jean Louis allegedly hid near a bush outside of the Walmart where Cooper worked, wearing a mask, and waited for her to end her night shift, according to Montgomery Country District Attorney Kevin Steele.
CALIFORNIA WOMAN CHASED, FATALLY SHOT BY ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT DOORDASH DRIVER WHO STALKED HER FOR MONTHS: DHS
"When Cooper left the store, he ran towards her and fatally shot her," according to court documents.

Court filings also revealed that Jean Louis, a former employee at the same Walmart who was terminated for immigration reasons, had previously physically assaulted Cooper and repeatedly contacted store staff to request Cooper's work schedule.
U.S. Marshals arrest Destino Jean Louis. (U.S. Marshals Service Philadelphia)

Prosecutors also determined from phone records that Jean Louis had taken multiple trips between his residence in Philadelphia and the Walmart location in Cheltenham in the weeks leading up to the shooting, the documents stated.

Jean Louis is being charged with murder in the first degree, murder in the third degree, illegal alien use of a firearm, carrying a firearm without a license and possession of an instrument with intent to commit a crime, according to court documents.

title: Ted Bundy linked to another decades-old homicide nearly 40 years after his execution
summary: DNA evidence has linked Ted Bundy to the 1974 murder of 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith, months after DNA tied him to Laura Ann Aime's killing.
story: Officials detail how DNA evidence tied serial killer Ted Bundy to the murder of 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith and closed the cold case 52 years after her body was found.
Utah authorities have identified notorious serial killer Ted Bundy as the killer of 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith, closing a homicide investigation 52 years to the day after her body was discovered.

Smith's body was found by hunters on Oct. 27, 1974, in a wooded area near the border of Summit and Salt Lake counties. Despite years of speculation, authorities never officially named a suspect and the case remained open for more than five decades.
The breakthrough came after DNA evidence in the killing of another 17-year-old Utah girl, Laura Ann Aime, produced a hit to Bundy in the Combined DNA Index System, or CODIS.

Investigators then compared DNA evidence from the Aime case with evidence preserved from Smith's killing and determined the profiles matched.

"This DNA evidence, when considered alongside evidence related to pattern, motive, means and opportunity, establishes that Ted Bundy was responsible for Melissa Ann Smith's murder," Summit County Attorney Margaret Olson said Tuesday.
The Smith investigation was revived after developments in Aime's case prompted Utah County investigators to contact Summit County in May 2025 about similarities between the two killings.
COLD-CASE FUGITIVE BUSTED SOUTH OF THE BORDER AS NEW DNA TECH ALLEGEDLY TIES HIM TO TEEN’S ROADSIDE KILLING
Aime vanished after leaving a Halloween party to buy cigarettes on Oct. 31, 1974. Her body was discovered by hikers near American Fork Canyon days later.
Investigators determined Aime had been raped, strangled and murdered.

title: Multi-state manhunt underway as murder victim's close friend fears escaped killer could strike again
summary: Jacob Allen Morley breached the Northwest Correctional Complex perimeter fence and stole a pickup truck, triggering a massive multi-state manhunt.
story: The best friend of Cody Birchfield says she fears for the public's safety after his convicted killer, Jacob Morley, escaped a Tennessee prison and triggered a multi-state manhunt.
The close friend of a Tennessee murder victim fears his convicted killer could strike again after escaping prison and triggering a multi-state manhunt.

Jacob Allen Morley escaped from the Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville, Tennessee, on Sunday, though officials have not said exactly when he got out. Prison staff discovered Morley was missing around 11:30 p.m., and a subsequent review of surveillance video showed him breaching the facility's perimeter fence.

Around 1 a.m. Monday, surveillance video captured Morley stealing a pickup truck from the 400 block of Keystone Drive, roughly two miles south of the prison, according to the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation. The white 2008 Ford F-350, bearing Tennessee license plate 138BBQV, has "Lindamood Planting Company" marked on its side.
TENNESSEE INMATE CONVICTED OF MURDER ESCAPES FROM PRISON, STEALS PICKUP TRUCK, MANHUNT UNDERWAY: OFFICIALS

Jacob Allen Morley, 28, was serving a life sentence for the 2022 murder of Cody Birchfield when he escaped from a Tennessee prison Sunday, according to correction officials. (Tennessee Department of Correction)
Morley was sentenced to life in prison after being convicted in 2025 of murdering Cody Birchfield three years earlier.
On Tuesday afternoon, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation said that the truck Morley stole was found abandoned in Marion, Illinois, but his location remains unknown.
Diana Reid, one of Birchfield's close childhood friends, told Fox News Digital that she's concerned Morley may hurt more people now that he's on the run.

"He's already been convicted of taking an innocent life. I believe he's extremely dangerous and I'm genuinely concerned that someone else could end up hurt if he's not caught soon," Reid said. "I'm genuinely scared knowing that someone convicted of such a violent crime is out there, not knowing where he's headed. What he's capable of doing next is just frightening."

Surveillance footage shows convicted murderer Jacob Allen Morley inside Northwest Correctional Complex before his escape Sunday. Authorities said Morley was captured on security video breaching a prison fence. (Tennessee Department of Correction)
"He’s got absolutely nothing to lose at this point and someone could become a victim just so he can continue his path to wherever he’s headed," she said.
Reid said Birchfield was "such a kind soul" and "had the biggest heart."
"He was more than just a murder victim, that he was someone who was deeply loved. He had a whole life ahead of him and he was completely robbed of that when he was murdered," Reid said.

title: Frustrated Illinois residents seek to redraw state map in bid to break free from Chicago
summary: Frustrated Illinois residents in 11 counties will vote on a non-binding referendum to break away from Cook County and form a new state in November.
story: Loret Newlin, director of Illinois Separation, discussed the push to form a new state amid frustration over Chicago's political influence and Illinois' criminal justice policies.

Frustrated Illinois residents are pushing to break away from Chicago and form a new state, driven by what the movement’s leader calls growing resentment over the city’s influence on the rest of Illinois.

Loret Newlin, director of Illinois Separation, which is leading the push to let voters weigh in on breaking away from Cook County and forming a new state, told Fox News Digital that residents outside the Chicago area are being ignored by state government and want to change that.
"Our area is not taken into consideration when laws are being made," Newlin said. "There's definitely more focus on them, and the laws are centered to benefit Chicago and Cook [County]."
‘VEXIT’ MOVEMENT REIGNITES AS RED STATE INVITES DISENFRANCHISED VIRGINIANS TO ‘BEST VIRGINIA’
Loret Newlin, director of Illinois Separation, told Fox News Digital that residents outside the Chicago area are being ignored by state government. (iStock)
"There is a lot of area outside of Cook that should have been taken into consideration," she said.

Newlin said that 11 counties and several townships in Illinois will vote on a non-binding referendum in November that asks residents if they'd be interested in separating from Cook County to form a new state.
TOP DEMOCRAT GOVERNORS ARE HOPING TO RIDE THEIR RECORDS TO THE WHITE HOUSE. CAN THEY?

Residents in some Illinois counties are pushing to separate from Cook County, where they feel Chicago has an outsized influence on the rest of the state. (Scott Olson/Getty Images; Marlin Levison/Star Tribune via Getty Images)

The referendums are intended to gauge whether voters want to pursue forming a separate state made up of Illinois counties outside Cook County. The effort draws on a process outlined in Article IV, Section 3 of the U.S. Constitution, the same provision invoked when West Virginia became a state in 1863.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB
She pointed to a proposed per-mile tax for drivers making its way through the Illinois legislature as one example of how she says state lawmakers are overlooking downstate residents.
SEND US A TIP
Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker holds a news conference in Chicago, Wednesday, June 24, 2026. (Terrence Antonio James/Chicago Tribune/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

Newlin said the proposed per-mile tax, introduced by state Sen. Ram Villivalam, whose district includes part of Chicago, would disproportionately affect rural residents, farmers and truckers who lack the public transit options available in the city.

"It's a long way to a lot of important things for people who live in downstate. A lot of our businesses rely on transportation. One of our biggest industries down here is truckers, farmers. And the commute to a job is usually a little farther, and we don't have the option of taking the Chicago public transit system," Newlin said. "And we tried to defeat this in 2019 and succeeded, but as typical, they won't take no for an answer."
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
Newlin also criticized Illinois' SAFE-T Act, saying she's "not happy" with the law and believes it "really benefits the criminals," and pointed to the impact it's having on Chicago.

Crime scene tape is stretched around the front of a home where a man was shot on May 28, 2017, in Chicago, Illinois. (Scott Olson/Getty Images)

The SAFE-T Act, signed into law by Democratic Gov. JB Pritzker in 2021, eliminated cash bail and established a new system for judges to determine whether defendants should be detained or released while awaiting trial.

Pritzker has opposed the idea of separation, and a spokesperson for his office previously called the movement a "stunt" that is "not going to happen," according to NBC Chicago.

title: Dems silent after violent attack in wealthy area of New York City as suspect remains at large
summary: The NYPD says a woman was raped at knifepoint inside Central Park as the suspect remains at large and the investigation continues in New York City.
story: A former NYPD inspector sounds the alarm after a woman was raped at knifepoint in Central Park. The attack comes amid a rise in reported rapes in the iconic park. Questions mount over public safety and the response from city and state leaders.

Top Democrats have been silent after the latest in a string of violent attacks in Central Park in New York City, where a suspect is at large after police say he sexually assaulted a woman at knifepoint.

A 39-year-old woman was raped in the park around 8:30 p.m. Saturday by a stranger who threatened her with a knife near the intersection of East 67th Street and East Drive, the NYPD said. It was the fifth reported rape in the NYPD’s Central Park Precinct this year, data show.

"This most recent rape was in an area that's right near $10 million apartments and an area where you would hope that people in this city would feel safe," said Paul Mauro, a retired NYPD inspector and Fox News contributor.

Two of the state’s top Democratic leaders, Gov. Kathy Hochul and Attorney General Letitia James, have so far remained silent on the attack — a stark contrast to their highly visible intervention earlier this month in a separate rape case involving seven Cornell fraternity members when Hochul swiftly appointed James as a special prosecutor.
The NYPD is searching for a suspect wanted in a rape that occurred in Central Park on Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026. (NYPD)

CORNELL SEXUAL ASSAULT CASE REVIVES SCRUTINY OF A LITTLE-KNOWN NEW YORK LAW ON INTOXICATED VICTIMS
"Let something hit the news like the Cornell case, and all of a sudden, they’re all over the media, and they’re on a soapbox, and they’re holding press conferences," Mauro said.

title: Feds crack down on stolen car pipeline to Mexican cartels as 13 charged in border scheme
summary: Operation Southbound Takedown recovered 29 stolen cars worth $1.14 million allegedly funneled through El Paso to Mexican cartels for daily operations.
story: Federal authorities announce charges against 13 people accused of transporting stolen vehicles across the border into Mexico for cartels. Credit: United States Attorneys' Offices.

A cross-border pipeline of stolen vehicles allegedly supplied Mexican cartels with cars and trucks to support their criminal operations, federal authorities say, with 13 people now facing charges in the scheme.

The vehicles were stolen from private owners and major rental car companies before being driven through El Paso, Texas, and across the border into Mexico, where they were allegedly used to support the cartels’ daily operations, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Texas.
Authorities have recovered 29 vehicles worth an estimated $1.14 million as part of the investigation, dubbed Operation Southbound Takedown, prosecutors said.
PIRRO WARNS CAR THEFT RING USED NEW TECH TO QUICKLY ACCESS VEHICLES: 'GONE IN 60 SECONDS'

Federal and local law enforcement officials announce charges in a stolen vehicle investigation during a press conference in El Paso, Texas, on Oct. 26, 2026. (U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Texas)
Ryan G. McRae, special agent in charge of Homeland Security Investigations in El Paso, said the stolen vehicles reveal a pattern of criminal activity extending beyond auto theft.

"These are not isolated property crimes," McRae said. "The stolen vehicles related to Operation Southbound Takedown demonstrate an alarming pattern and are used to support the day-to-day operations of dangerous criminal organizations."
Photos released by prosecutors showed a damaged white SUV recovered in Mexico, as well as an armored black SUV and an armored pickup truck.

Federal agents and prosecutors began investigating in the spring after identifying a pattern of stolen vehicles being transported to individuals allegedly connected to criminal organizations in Mexico, the U.S. attorney’s office said.
NEVADA MAN FUNNELED 140 GUNS TO VIOLENT MEXICAN DRUG CARTELS, INCLUDING POWERFUL 'MILITARY-STYLE' RIFLES: DOJ

Authorities released a photo of an armored SUV recovered during an investigation into stolen vehicles allegedly transported from the U.S. to criminal organizations in Mexico. (U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Texas)

U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons warned people considering transporting stolen vehicles into Mexico that cartels are exploiting individuals looking to make a "quick buck" to further their criminal operations.
Those operations, he said, include "human smuggling, extortion, drug trafficking and even murder."
TRUMP ADMIN'S LIST OF US-DESIGNATED 'FOREIGN TERRORIST' GROUPS IN LATIN AMERICA EXPANDS TO 21

"You are now on notice," Simmons said. "If you provide support to these cartels, many of which have been designated as foreign terrorist organizations, by transporting stolen vehicles out of this country and into Mexico, we will find you, and we will prosecute to the fullest extent of the law."

Of the 13 people charged, 11 are U.S. citizens and two are Mexican citizens, prosecutors said. One of the Mexican citizens has a lawful permanent resident card, while the other has a border crossing card.
Two of the Americans, Kimberly Aguilar and Marty Gerardo Jr., are in state custody. The other 11 people were federally indicted and arrested between July 22 and Oct. 19, according to prosecutors.

All 13 are charged with interstate transportation of stolen property and face up to 10 years in federal prison if convicted. The charges are allegations, and each person is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.
An armored black pickup truck was recovered as part of Operation Southbound Takedown. (U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Texas)
The investigation involved Homeland Security Investigations, the FBI and other federal, state and local agencies working through the Homeland Security Task Force.
McRae said authorities worked with private-sector partners to disrupt the alleged vehicle theft and transportation network as part of an investigation spanning the United States and Mexico.

"This work is ongoing; we’re not stopping here," he said.
FBI El Paso Acting Special Agent in Charge Coult W. Markovsky also had a warning for people helping cartels.
"To individuals assisting the cartels, Justice will find you!" he said.

title: Florida mom arrested after Vegas trip left 4 kids without overnight supervision: deputies
summary: Body camera video shows deputies arresting Irene Miller at the airport after her four children were found home alone while she was in Las Vegas.
story: Bodycam video shows deputies meeting Irene Miller as she exits a flight from Las Vegas and arresting her after they say she left her four children home alone. Credit: Osceola County Sheriff’s Office.
A Florida mother returning from Las Vegas was met by deputies as she stepped off a plane and was arrested after authorities say she left her four children home alone while she traveled for work.
Body camera video shows deputies approaching Irene Miller as she exited the plane Friday morning, escorting her through the airport terminal and placing her in handcuffs.
The arrest came two days after one of Miller’s children called 911 to report that a dumbbell had fallen on her 9-year-old brother’s head, according to the Osceola County Sheriff’s Office.
FLORIDA AG SEEKS DEATH PENALTY FOR COUPLE WHO ALLEGEDLY HELD 4 CHILDREN IN ‘ROLLING PRISON’ FOR NEARLY 7 YEARS
Irene Miller, 50, was arrested Oct. 23, 2026, on four counts of child neglect, according to the Osceola County Sheriff’s Office. (Osceola County Sheriff's Office)

Deputies responded to the Kissimmee home shortly after 8:30 p.m. on Oct. 21 and found four children, ages 9, 11, 12 and 14, with no adults present, the sheriff’s office said. Fire rescue crews took the injured boy to Celebration Hospital, where he was treated and discharged.
A deputy reached Miller by phone, and she said she was working in Las Vegas and planned to return Oct. 23, according to the sheriff’s office. Deputies learned she had left Florida on Oct. 18.
FLORIDA 3-YEAR-OLD DIES AFTER TRAGIC INCIDENT INVOLVING COMMON PLAY TOY AT BABYSITTER'S HOUSE

Deputies approached Irene Miller on the jet bridge after her flight from Las Vegas landed Oct. 23, 2026. The Osceola County Sheriff’s Office said she had traveled there for work. (Osceola County Sheriff's Office)

Miller told deputies she had arranged for a babysitter to travel from Tampa in the mornings to help the children get ready for school and check on them afterward. The sitter was not required to stay overnight, the sheriff’s office said.
Authorities contacted the children’s father, who agreed to take all four to his home while detectives made plans to meet Miller when her flight landed.
SAN JOSE GIRL, 8, DIES AFTER LIVING IN COCKROACH-INFESTED HOME AS MOTHER, STEPFATHER FACE CHARGES
Body camera video shows Irene Miller being escorted outside the airport in handcuffs on Oct. 23, 2026. She was charged with four counts of child neglect. (Osceola County Sheriff's Office)
Deputies arrested Miller, 50, on four counts of child neglect without great bodily harm and booked her into the Orange County Jail.

"The Osceola County Sheriff’s Office will not tolerate child neglect," Sheriff Chris Blackmon said. "These cases will be investigated, and charges will be brought against the parents who are not properly supervising or caring for their children."

title: Middle school teacher arrested in alleged prostitution scheme at casino hotel
summary: The Middle Township Middle School teacher was fired after allegedly helping restrain a man during a prostitution-related robbery in a casino hotel room.
story: Middle Township Middle School teacher Amanda Crafts was fired after allegedly helping restrain a man during a prostitution-related robbery at an Atlantic City casino hotel. (Google Maps)
A New Jersey teacher was arrested two weeks ago in connection with an alleged prostitution scheme in which a man was restrained, forced to endure sexual acts and robbed in a casino hotel room.

The suspect was identified as Amanda Crafts, 35, of Wildwood Crest, according to the New Jersey Department of Corrections. She was a computer teacher at Middle Township Middle School, according to her LinkedIn.
Her friend, Veda Engel, 23, of Cape May, was also charged in the Oct. 9 incident. Engel has a history of prostitution-related charges, including one dating back to December, Breaking AC reported.
FLORIDA WOMAN ALLEGEDLY DRUGS MAN SHE MET AT CLUB, STEALS HIS NEARLY $100K ROLEX: POLICE
According to police, the victim met the women at a bar at a hotel resort in Atlantic City, the outlet said.
After exchanging numbers with Engel, he reportedly met the two women in their room.
MANHATTAN PROSTITUTE PLEADS GUILTY TO KILLING 3 MEN WITH FENTANYL-LACED DRUGS IN ROBBERY SCHEME
Once inside, the victim said the two women stripped him down and physically restrained him to the bed, the outlet reported.
Engel then forced sexual acts on him before stopping and saying, "That’s what you get for $1,250," according to the complaint, Breaking AC reported.
As Crafts held the victim down, Engel reportedly used his facial recognition to unlock his phone and made four separate Apple Pay transactions totaling $1,250 to her account.
Two women were arrested in connection with an alleged prostitution-related robbery at an Atlantic City casino hotel on Oct. 9, 2026. (Bruce Bennett/Getty Images)
The victim said the transactions were "made without his consent in exchange for sexual acts," a detective wrote in the affidavits, according to reports.
During her first appearance in court, Crafts told the judge that she was a teacher and had never been arrested before.
"I was in the wrong place at the wrong time," she told Judge Timothy Maguire during a video appearance from the Atlantic County Justice Facility, according to reports.
FLORIDA MIDDLE SCHOOL TEACHER ADMITS TO YEARS OF 'INAPPROPRIATE' CONVERSATIONS WITH FORMER STUDENT: DEPUTIES
Crafts, who said she has four children, works in the school’s special area department teaching computers, the outlet said, citing the school’s website.
The school district released a statement on Oct. 19 acknowledging the arrest of a Middle Township teacher and confirming that the employee had been fired.

"Our responsibility is to protect our students, follow appropriate procedures and ensure that those entrusted with caring for and educating our children meet the standards expected of them. The safety and well-being of our students remain our highest priority," Superintendent Stephanie DeRose said.
Middle Township Public Schools announced the teacher’s firing in a community message, emphasizing the safety and well-being of its students. (Middle Township School District/Facebook)
Separately, Engel works at SoFresh SoClean Commercial Cleaning in Ocean City, her attorney said, according to Breaking AC.

The incident was not Engel’s first prostitution-related encounter with law enforcement. Last year, she allegedly offered an undercover New Jersey State Police detective sex in exchange for $1,000 at the Borgata Hotel Casino & Spa.
She was reportedly released on a summons at the time.

title: Stranded hikers cling to steep California mountain ridge as helicopter crew swoops in
summary: Three people trapped on a Northern California cliff were hoisted by helicopter after a Garmin inReach SOS alerted Sierra County authorities.
story: A rescue helicopter returns after three people stranded on a steep section of California’s Sierra Buttes were lifted to safety. Credit: Sierra County Sheriff's Office
Three people stranded high on a steep Northern California mountainside were rescued by helicopter Sunday after a distress call brought crews racing to their aid.
The Sierra County Sheriff’s Office said the group was found on the Sierra Buttes, just south of a lookout tower near the mountain’s summit.
Images and video released by officials show the helicopter near the rugged mountainside as rescuers worked to reach the trio.
HELICOPTER RESCUE CREW CAUGHT ON CAMERA SAVING 2 CLIMBERS TRAPPED ALONG POPULAR CALIFORNIA BEACH CLIFF

A rescue helicopter flies near the Sierra Buttes during an operation to reach three people stranded on a steep section of the Northern California mountain on Oct. 25, 2026. (Sierra County Sheriff's Office)
The sheriff’s office was alerted around 2:30 p.m. after a Garmin inReach satellite communication device sent an SOS signal to the California Governor’s Office of Emergency Services.
Deputies launched a search and rescue response and called in the Nevada County Sheriff’s Search and Rescue Mountain Rescue Team and the Washoe County Sheriff’s Office’s RAVEN helicopter crew.
TOURISTS SEEKING 'DRAMATIC' PHOTO ON ISOLATED BEACH TRAPPED BY INCOMING TIDE
The Washoe County Sheriff’s Office RAVEN helicopter responds to a rescue on the Sierra Buttes, where three people were stranded on steep terrain on Oct. 25, 2026. (Sierra County Sheriff's Office)

Once the crew spotted the stranded group, a rescue team member was lowered from the helicopter to reach them. All three were then hoisted off the mountainside and flown to a landing zone, where Sierra County deputies were waiting.
"Due to the difficult terrain and hazardous location, a helicopter hoist rescue was necessary," the sheriff’s office said.
NORTH CAROLINA CLIMBER AIRLIFTED AFTER PLUNGING 20 FEET DOWN GORGE, SUSTAINING SERIOUS INJURIES
The Washoe County Sheriff’s Office RAVEN helicopter sits on a paved landing area during a rescue operation on the Sierra Buttes in California on Oct. 25, 2026. (Sierra County Sheriff's Office)
The agency thanked the teams involved for their "professionalism, coordination, and assistance" in bringing the rescue to a successful conclusion.
The Sierra Buttes rise above the North Yuba River canyon, with a fire lookout near the top of the approximately 8,600-foot mountain, according to the Pacific Crest Trail Association.
Authorities did not say how the three people became stranded or whether anyone was injured.
The rescue drew praise on social media, where commenters thanked the emergency crews and pointed to the RAVEN helicopter team’s role in helping communities across the region.
"To see that Sheriff Balaam uses the RAVEN team to assist anywhere they are needed is outstanding and certainly shows just how valuable the unit has become to the region," one person wrote.
Another thanked the rescue teams, writing, "Really awesome work, coordination and knowledge by all involved. Impressive and grateful to have this in our community."
"Hats off to our emergency special teams!!" another commenter wrote. "We are all very fortunate that you all do what you do."
The dramatic rescue came after two other high-profile rescues on Northern California mountains earlier this month.

Last week, a 39-year-old Florida man was flown to a hospital after he fell through a snow bridge and severely injured his leg on the Whitney Glacier. Crews ultimately carried him to a viable helicopter landing zone the next day, the Siskiyou County Sheriff’s Office said.

title: West Virginia couple charged after kids found in alleged 'house of horrors'
summary: Authorities said the three children were removed from the home after investigators uncovered disturbing allegations of yearslong abuse and neglect.
story: Erica Sayre faces three counts of child abuse resulting in bodily injury and three counts of child neglect creating risk of injury.  (Jackson County Sheriff's Office)

A West Virginia couple is facing felony charges after authorities said three children endured years of alleged abuse and neglect inside what the local sheriff described as a real-life "house of horrors."

Erica Lynn Sayre, 45, and her husband, Clifford Gale Sayre, 46, both of Evans, were charged following an "extensive investigation" by the Jackson County Sheriff's Department, authorities announced Monday.

Erica and Clifford Sayre each face six felony charges, including three counts of child neglect creating risk of injury. Erica Sayre also faces three counts of child abuse resulting in bodily injury, while Clifford Sayre faces three counts of child neglect resulting in bodily injury.
Authorities alleged the children were repeatedly struck and strangled, deprived of food and water and denied access to the bathroom.
TENNESSEE INMATE CONVICTED OF MURDER ESCAPES FROM PRISON, MANHUNT UNDERWAY: OFFICIALS
Investigators also alleged that soiled cat litter was dumped in their beds, dog feces was placed on their belongings and they were forced to run barefoot on a gravel driveway as punishment.
The children were also allegedly struck with household objects, forced to put a soiled sock in their mouths and subjected to having their hair forcibly cut.

"One child described being struck in the head with an electronic device, causing a bleeding injury for which she was denied medical treatment. One of the children was threatened to be killed if she contacted Child Protective Services," the sheriff's office alleged.
During interviews, one child became emotional and told investigators, "I can't go back to that home," the sheriff's department said. Another said she "just wants a normal life."
TEEN ACCUSED OF STEPSISTER’S CRUISE SHIP MURDER BUYS TIME TO CONSIDER PLEA BUT WON’T GET ‘SWEET’ DEAL: EXPERT
Clifford Sayre faces three counts of child neglect resulting in bodily injury and three counts of child neglect creating risk of injury. (Jackson County Sheriff's Office)
Investigators alleged Clifford Sayre witnessed repeated abuse but failed to intervene. One child claimed he restrained her hands while Erica Sayre cut her hair with a razor blade, causing an injury.
"Because mom hits us and Gale lets her," the children said during a forensic interview, according to the sheriff's department.
Authorities said investigators worked with Child Protective Services and a Child Advocacy Center and documented scars that were consistent with portions of the children's accounts.
Investigators said the children's statements also corroborated one another and other physical evidence collected during the investigation.
All of the children were removed from the home after the allegations were disclosed, according to authorities.
The investigation included multiple interviews, medical examinations and photographic evidence.

"The Jackson County Sheriff's Department emphasizes the seriousness of allegations involving child abuse and neglect of vulnerable children and remains committed to investigating such reports thoroughly and efficiently," Sheriff Ross Mellinger said in a statement.

title: Illegal alien pleads guilty to staging fake kidnapping to target Border Patrol
summary: Yuriana Julia Pelaez Calderón allegedly fabricated her abduction, altered her appearance and hid in California to build a lawsuit against Border Patrol.
story: ‘The Big Weekend Show’ co-host Joey Jones breaks down deportation numbers and illegal immigration enforcement data under the Trump administration.

Federal officials on Monday announced that an illegal alien from Mexico pleaded guilty to staging a fake kidnapping in 2025, falsely claiming she had been abducted by federal agents or people acting on their behalf.

Yuriana Julia Pelaez Calderón, 43, of South Los Angeles, fabricated her disappearance to stir media outrage and build a case for a lawsuit against Border Patrol before going into hiding, according to the Office of First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bilal A. Essayli for the Central District of California.
"In June and July of 2025, Calderón faked her apprehension by federal agents or surrogates acting on behalf of federal agents," officials said.
According to the attorney’s office, Calderón repeatedly contacted individuals using anonymous and blocked phone calls to build a fraudulent narrative.
MEXICAN WOMAN IN US ILLEGALLY CHARGED WITH FAKING HER OWN ICE ‘KIDNAPPING’
Photos allegedly staged to make Yuriana Julia Pelaez Calderon appear to have been detained and mistreated in custody, according to an affidavit. (US Department of Justice)

She falsely claimed federal agents had abducted and detained her at multiple locations, officials said. As she staged her release, she also altered her appearance to make it appear as though she had been mistreated in custody.

Court documents show that on June 25, 2025, Calderón falsely told an individual that immigration officials were taking her into custody near a fast-food restaurant and claimed agents had threatened to break her window.

Two days later, Calderón reportedly used caller ID blocking to contact a tenants' rights advocate with another false claim. She allegedly lied that authorities had taken her to San Ysidro and forced her to sign deportation papers.
AI VOICE SCAM TRAPS MOM IN 5-HOUR KIDNAPPING NIGHTMARE
Yuriana Julia Pelaez Calderon is seen in surveillance video at a parking lot. (Justice Department)
That same day, she reportedly told another individual that she had been moved to an unknown warehouse, where she was being held with other detainees.

"As a result of Calderón’s intentional lies, false information was reported to the media and law enforcement that Calderón had been ‘kidnapped’ by masked men in plain clothes driving an unmarked vehicle, who were acting as federal agents or as surrogates of federal agents," officials said.
While Calderón "chose to stay hidden in Bakersfield," her false claims prompted community organizers to demand her release, according to officials.

title: College homecoming party turns to chaos as deck collapses, leaving at least 28 people injured
summary: A back deck collapsed during a William & Mary homecoming party in Williamsburg, Virginia, injuring at least 28 people at an off-campus home.
story: Images show a collapsed deck at a Williamsburg, Virginia, home near William & Mary’s campus after at least 28 people were injured during an off-campus homecoming party. Credit: City of Williamsburg

A college homecoming party took a frightening turn Friday night when a back deck collapsed at a Virginia home, leaving at least 28 people injured and sending emergency crews rushing to the neighborhood.
William & Mary confirmed students were among those injured at the off-campus residence in Williamsburg. All reported injuries were non-life-threatening, according to city officials.
Dispatchers received a report of a structure collapse around 10:07 p.m. on the 200 block of Matoaka Court. Responding police and firefighters found the home’s back deck had collapsed, the city said.
TERRIFYING SCENE UNFOLDS AS METAL CABANA FRAME CRASHES INTO PACKED CASINO POOL AREA
A collapsed wooden deck sits behind police tape at a Williamsburg, Virginia, home after a homecoming party incident injured at least 28 people Oct. 23, 2026. (City of Williamsburg)
Emergency crews took 13 people to hospitals, while another 15 reportedly sought treatment on their own, according to the city’s Saturday morning update.
Neighbors told WAVY that a homecoming party was underway when the deck gave way. One described emergency vehicles stretching through the neighborhood.

"All the way down the street and wrapped around just ambulances and fire trucks," the neighbor, who asked not to be named, told WAVY. "We saw a lot of hospital gurneys coming out of ambulances. At least nine ambulances kind of wrapped around the street."
WATCH: VIRGINIA COPS CRAWL THROUGH BURNING HOUSE TO SAVE MAN TRAPPED IN FIRE

A view of William & Mary’s campus in Williamsburg, Virginia. The university confirmed students were among those injured when a deck collapsed at an off-campus home Oct. 23, 2026. (Jeffrey Greenberg/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

Joshua Wise, who lives next to the home, told the outlet some of his classmates were involved. He returned after emergency crews had finished responding but learned his housemate had been helping people get home.

"Word was traveling pretty fast," Wise told WAVY. "By the time I got back here, the emergency response was over, but I had a housemate who was helping people, trying to help out as much as possible, drive people home, get people where they needed to be."
Wise credited neighbors with coming together after the frightening incident.
"We did everything we could to help each other out and I think that that’s beautiful," he said.
5 VICTIMS RELEASED FROM HOSPITAL AFTER FLORIDA A&M UNIVERSITY SHOOTING, 1 REMAINS CRITICAL
William & Mary offered support to students injured in an off-campus deck collapse during homecoming weekend. (Alex Perry/Virginia Gazette/The Virginian-Pilot/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

In a Saturday message to the campus community, William & Mary’s senior vice president for student affairs and public safety, Ginger Ambler, said the university was still gathering information. Additional students may have sought care beyond those initially counted, she noted.
"We are grateful that none of the injuries were life-threatening," Ambler wrote.
College of William & Mary on Monday, October 25, 2021, in Williamsburg, Virginia. (Getty Images)
She said staff across the university’s health, academic and student support offices were working to assist affected students.
"We recognize that such an experience may affect our students deeply and in different ways," Ambler wrote.
Wise also praised the emergency response.
"Thank goodness for the emergency responders," he told WAVY. "They were great. The ambulances and everything got here pretty fast."

Local police and firefighters responded, and city officials were working with area hospitals to confirm the total number of people treated.
The city’s Codes Compliance Division is evaluating and inspecting the site.

title: Stolen car slams into South Carolina home as teens bolt, authorities say
summary: Video shows a stolen car slamming into a South Carolina home before two teenagers fled, prompting Greenville County deputies to deploy K9s and a drone.
story: Video shows a reported stolen car crashing into a Simpsonville home before a search involving deputies, K9 teams and a drone. Two teens were arrested, and no injuries were reported. Credit: Greenville County Sheriff's Office
A stolen car barreled through neighborhood yards and smashed into a South Carolina home before two teenagers ran, triggering a search involving deputies, K9 teams and a drone, authorities said.
Video released by the Greenville County Sheriff’s Office shows the car slamming into the house before deputies rush toward the wreck and chase a fleeing suspect.
"Is everybody alright?" a deputy can be heard asking as authorities check the home for anyone who might be hurt.
FOUR TEENS KILL COUPLE IN HEAD-ON CRASH AFTER STEALING G-WAGON, LEADING COPS ON HOURS-LONG CHASE: POLICE
A deputy rushes toward a Simpsonville home after a reported stolen vehicle crashed into it Oct. 15, 2026. Authorities said two teenagers were arrested. (Greenville County Sheriff's Office)

The sheriff’s office said deputies attempted to stop the reported stolen vehicle around 2:30 p.m. Oct. 15. The driver fled, but deputies said they did not pursue the car before it crashed into the home on Renwood Road in Simpsonville.
Two teenagers, ages 15 and 16, were eventually arrested and charged with possession of a stolen vehicle, authorities said. No injuries were reported.
WATCH: DEPUTIES HUNT WANTED MAN THROUGH CORNFIELD AFTER HIGH-SPEED CHASE CAUGHT ON CAMERA
A reported stolen vehicle sits amid damage to a home on Renwood Road in Simpsonville, South Carolina, on Oct. 15, 2026. No injuries were reported. (Greenville County Sheriff's Office)

The video shows one deputy running after a fleeing suspect while another heads toward the damaged home. The passenger was quickly taken into custody, while the search for the driver brought help from above and on the ground.

K9 teams used multiple dogs to track the driver’s path, and drone operators provided an aerial view of the neighborhood, according to the sheriff’s office. The video also shows a dog picking up a scent collected from the vehicle before tracking the driver.
BLOODHOUND K-9 UNIT HELPS BRING GEORGIA MANHUNT TO END WITH ARREST OF SUSPECT ACCUSED OF SHOOTING WOMAN

A teen sits handcuffed in a patrol vehicle after the Oct. 15, 2026, incident. Deputies said two teenagers, ages 15 and 16, were charged with possession of a stolen vehicle. (Greenville County Sheriff's Office)

"When someone decides to run from law enforcement in Greenville County, they quickly learn that our deputies have more than one way to find them," the sheriff’s office wrote in a post accompanying the video.
"You can run, but our deputies have a pretty impressive toolbox. And they know how to use it," the agency added.
For neighbors, the crash brought a frightening interruption to an otherwise routine afternoon.
"I was just putting my baby down for a nap, and I heard a big crash outside," next-door neighbor Rachel Bush told WYFF.
Just minutes earlier, Bush said, she had been walking outside with her baby and dog.
"We were grateful we were back inside before everything happened," she told the outlet.
DRIVER RELEASED WITHOUT CHARGES AFTER PICKUP KILLS BOY, 6, AND MAN ON KANSAS SOCCER FIELD
One of the home’s residents told WYFF that no one was home when the car crashed through the front door. He and his fiancé returned from an errand minutes later to find the damage.
The resident said the car missed another vehicle in the garage by inches, leaving behind an extensive cleanup and repair job.
Another neighbor, Robert Belcher, told WYFF he offered support after seeing what happened.
"I don’t know what to say to you but thank God no one was at home," Belcher recalled telling his neighbor.

The resident also offered a pointed message to the teenagers accused in the incident.
"Think about what you are doing; you never know if it’s going to impact lives," he told WYFF.

title: Israelis vote in record numbers in first national election since the Oct. 7 Hamas massacre
summary: Israel election exit polls show Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud and Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar locked in a fight with neither bloc reaching 61 Knesset seats.
story: Fox News chief foreign correspondent Trey Yingst reports as Israelis vote in the first national election since the Oct. 7 attacks and the start of the Iran war, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu facing a tight race.

TEL AVIV, Israel — Israelis turned out in exceptionally high numbers Tuesday for the country’s first national election since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas massacre, with initial exit polls showing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud emerging as the largest party but his governing coalition falling short of a parliamentary majority, potentially opening the door to a change in leadership.

The projections released by Israel’s three major television networks after polls closed at 10 p.m. local time (4 p.m. ET) showed Likud winning 25 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, compared with 23 seats for former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party in Channels 12 and 13 exit polls, and 21 seats according to Kan 11.

The projected parliamentary balance showed 50 seats for Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc, 53 for the main opposition parties and 17 for Arab parties, leaving neither major bloc with the 61 seats generally needed to form a government.

Although Netanyahu’s party is projected to remain the largest in parliament, his political future is far from secure. The opposition parties, together with the Arab factions, would hold a combined 70 seats, although that does not mean they would necessarily agree to form a government together.
FORMER ISRAELI ARMY CHIEF GADI EISENKOT EMERGES AS NETANYAHU’S LEADING ELECTION CHALLENGER
A polling station in Herzliya, Israel, on Oct. 27, 2026, as Israelis head to the polls in the country's first national election since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas massacre. (Efrat Lachter)
The results set the stage for potentially weeks of coalition negotiations, with the possibility that Netanyahu could lose power despite Likud finishing first.
Netanyahu fights for political future as Israel heads to polls with Iran threat looming
The results are preliminary projections, not an official vote count, and could change as ballots are tallied in the coming days.
The election followed an extraordinary day at polling stations across Israel, with long lines and voter participation reaching levels not seen in decades.

Israeli voter turnout surged to a historic high, with 55.7% of eligible voters casting their ballots by 4 p.m. local time (10 a.m. ET), according to Israel's Central Elections Committee. The figure marked the highest turnout recorded at that hour since measurements began in 1973, underscoring the intensity of the country's national election.

The unusually high participation prompted election officials to streamline voting procedures and assure voters that anyone arriving at a polling station before the 10 p.m. deadline would be allowed to cast a ballot.

The vote was widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu's leadership following three years of war and continuing questions about responsibility for the security failures that allowed Hamas terrorists to kill approximately 1,200 people and abduct 251 others on Oct. 7, 2023.
JD VANCE DECLINES TO ENDORSE NETANYAHU DESPITE TRUMP'S STRONG BACKING

Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, campaigned on his record of confronting Iran and its regional proxies, highlighting Israel's military achievements and his relationship with President Donald Trump.His opponents accused him of failing to accept responsibility for the October 7 security failures and opposed his government's approach to investigating the failures that preceded the massacre.
A last-minute battle for every vote

Throughout the final hours of the campaign, Netanyahu, Eisenkot, former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett and other party leaders mounted an intensive effort to mobilize supporters and win over undecided voters.
Netanyahu's Likud party prepared hundreds of targeted campaign videos and social media messages, making digital outreach a central part of its last-minute election strategy.
Eisenkot's campaign pushed supporters to rally behind Yashar as the leading alternative to Likud, while Bennett traveled between cities and engaged voters directly and through WhatsApp conversations.
NETANYAHU FIGHTS FOR POLITICAL FUTURE AS ISRAEL HEADS TO POLLS WITH IRAN THREAT LOOMING
Former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot attends an event for his Yashar party, ahead of Israel's national election in Tel Aviv, Israel, October 25, 2026. (Ronen Zvulun/Reuters)
The campaign's closing hours also featured personal appeals, phone calls to undecided voters and aggressive turnout operations across the political spectrum.
The final days were particularly important because a relatively small share of voters remained undecided about which party to support.

A Times of Israel poll published five days before the election found that 87% of respondents had already made their final choice, while 2.4% remained undecided between the pro- and anti-Netanyahu political blocs.
Other surveys suggested a larger pool of undecided voters, although many were choosing between parties within the same political camp rather than switching sides.
That distinction could prove decisive in Israel's parliamentary system, where political parties need at least 3.25% of valid votes to enter the 120-seat Knesset.
Even a slight change in the vote share of smaller parties could shift several parliamentary seats and determine whether either camp has a realistic path to power.
TRUMP SAYS NETANYAHU NEEDS TO BE RE-ELECTED, OR ELSE US WILL HAVE TO 'FINISH THE JOB’ AGAINST IRAN ALONE
A boy sits on his bicycle next to a campaign banner of Netanyahu's Likud party, ahead of the Israeli parliamentary election, in Bnei Brak, Israel, October 25, 2026. (Nir Elias/Reuters)
What happens next?
Despite the exit poll projections, the identity of Israel's next prime minister may remain uncertain for weeks.
Unlike in the United States, Israelis vote for political parties rather than directly electing their head of government.
The 120 seats in parliament are allocated proportionally, and parties must secure at least 3.25% of valid votes to win representation.

Once the final results are certified, Israeli President Isaac Herzog will consult with the newly elected political factions and select the lawmaker he believes has the strongest chance of forming a government.
That candidate will have 28 days to negotiate a governing coalition, with the possibility of a 14-day extension.

A woman looks on as people attend a rally to demand the establishment of an independent state commission of inquiry into the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attacks and the events leading up to them, ahead of Israel's parliamentary election on October 27, in Tel Aviv, Israel, October 24, 2026. (Nir Elias/Reuters)
Official results are scheduled to be published by Nov. 4. Until a new government takes office, Netanyahu's outgoing government will remain in power.

Lachter’s reporting has taken her into conflict zones and crisis areas across the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Africa. Her work has included uncovering human trafficking networks, revealing an ISIS underground torture prison in Syria, documenting the war in Ukraine and interviewing senior political figures and world leaders. She was also among the Western journalists who entered Russia after the war began to bring testimonies from Putin’s opposition. title: Sen Flávio Bolsonaro reportedly flees Brazil for US after election loss
summary: The Brazilian far-right senator has reportedly headed to Florida two days after losing the presidential runoff to leftist incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
story: Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro joined supporters in Santa Barbara D'Oeste, Brazil, to lead a motorcade. Polls in Brazil show a tight presidential race with incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. (Reuters)

Brazilian Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro has reportedly left Brazil for the United States on Tuesday, two days after losing the country's presidential runoff to leftist incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
An ally of the far-right conservative senator confirmed his departure to Reuters on Tuesday.
Bolsonaro's flight is reportedly headed to Florida, according to Brazilian outlet Metropoles, citing people close to his family.
The 45-year-old lawmaker had been out of public view since Tuesday morning, the outlet reported.
BRAZIL’S RAPID ELECTION COUNT PUTS SPOTLIGHT ON VOTING SECURITY AHEAD OF US MIDTERMS
Brazilian Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro reportedly left Brazil for the U.S. on Tuesday after losing his bid to become the nation's next president. (Evaristo Sa / AFP via Getty Images)

His reported departure came as a deadline for him to surrender his regular and diplomatic passports expired at noon Tuesday. Brazilian newspaper Folha de São Paulo reported Bolsonaro was under investigation for alleged money laundering and other crimes.
It remained unclear whether Bolsonaro had complied with the order, The Associated Press reported.
Bolsonaro was served with the order Monday, one day after Lula defeated him in Sunday's presidential runoff.
BRAZIL BECOMES NEXT TEST FOR LATIN AMERICA’S SURGING CONSERVATIVE MOVEMENT
With 100% of the vote counted, Lula won 51.8% of the vote. (Amanda Perobelli/Reuters)
With 100% of the vote counted, Lula won 51.8% of the vote, defeating Bolsonaro by nearly 4.4 million votes.
He has refused to concede the election and has called for the election results to be annulled, alleging fraud, according to The Associated Press.
Lula addressed supporters after winning re-election to a fourth, nonconsecutive term, expressing gratitude to the Brazilian people.
CONSERVATIVE WAVE HITS ROADBLOCK IN BRAZIL AS LULA HOLDS OFF BOLSONARO CHALLENGE
Lula addressed supporters after winning re-election to a fourth, nonconsecutive term, expressing gratitude to the Brazilian people. (Diego Vara/Reuters)
"No one is required to like the president-elect, but he must govern for everyone," Lula said.

Referring to his opponent, Lula said, "This was a defeat for denialism and lies."
The White House could not immediately be reached by Fox News Digital for comment.
Fox News Digital's David Unsworth and Michael Sinkewicz, as well as Reuters and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Serbia’s student movement topples Vucic’s party after 14 years, but political agenda remains unclear
summary: Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat to the Student List after a landslide victory ended his 14-year rule over Serbia in a historic election day.
story: Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in snap parliamentary elections after a student-led protest movement mounted the biggest challenge to his rule in more than a decade. (Reuters.)
Serbia’s longtime leader, President Aleksandar Vucic, conceded defeat Sunday to the student-led opposition in an election that sent shock waves throughout Europe and the Western Balkans.

"We do not have the final results yet, and many people will be surprised. Based on a stratified sample, it is clear that we have lost these elections. The student-led protest list has won," Vucic said in an address to the nation Sunday night.

The Student List victory brings an end to 14 years of Vucic and his Serbian Progressive Party rule, in what many are saying is the biggest political shake-up in the Balkans since the toppling of Yugoslav dictator Slobodan Milosevic in 2000.
Observers say the Student List party's policies remain vague, which has some worried about Serbia's future.

Ana Brnabic, vice president of the main Board of the Serbian Progressive Party, told Fox News Digital that, "The election victory of the Student List recalls similar electoral triumphs in other countries. The Student List represents a classical anti-establishment movement: it had neither a program nor a coherent political ideology. In an essentially anarchic fashion, it opposed everything, claiming to fight for justice and against corruption."
ANTI‑CORRUPTION PROTESTS HIT EUROPEAN NATION AS CALLS FOR NEW ELECTIONS GROW

Serbia's former President and the ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) candidate for Prime Minister Aleksandar Vucic gestures during a pre-election rally at King Milan Square in Nis, Serbia, Oct. 21, 2026.  (Djordje Kojadinovic/Reuters)

She added, "After 14 years of Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) rule, people may have wanted change. That is understandable and logical. But the grim consequences of this movement in power will soon become apparent."
Turnout reached 69 %, the highest this century, with more than 4.4 million people casting their ballots, according to Rasa Nedeljkov, head of the CRTA Election Observation Mission.

"This is by all means a historic victory and indeed a surprise to many. While it was clear from the beginning that the students will have an impressive result, very few expected a landslide," Helena Ivanov, associate fellow at the Henry Jackson Society, told Fox News Digital.

The Election Observation Mission reported that the Student List won 52.45 % of the vote and is projected to hold 138 of 250 seats in the National Assembly, an absolute majority, allowing it to form a government on its own.
Vucic won 39.2 % and is projected to hold 103 seats.
Supporters celebrated throughout Belgrade and across Serbia as it became clear the Student List won by a larger margin that caught many experts and observers by surprise.

Many claimed they were concerned about the possibility of violence escalating as polls began to close. Almost two hours after polling stations closed, Vucic addressed the nation, confirming his defeat and announcing the peaceful transfer of power.
FRANCE ROCKED BY STUDENT RIOTS AS HUNDREDS ARRESTED, VIOLENCE SPREADS NATIONWIDE

Students walk on the road towards the northern city of Novi Sad, where they will participate in a 24 hour block of three bridges to protest the deaths of 15 people killed in the November collapse of a train station canopy, near the Belgrade suburb of Batajnica, Serbia, Thursday, Jan. 30, 2025.  (AP Photo/Darko Vojinovic)

"The path to an electoral victory with such a decisive margin will undoubtedly earn its own chapter in the handbooks on how to topple an autocrat. Two years of unprecedented grassroots mobilization, creative organization and impeccable campaigning kept the student list two steps ahead of the regime. Vučić was left playing catch-up, and all his attempts to co-opt, demoralize and fragment the movement failed," Sinisa Vukovic, director of the Global Policy Program at the School of Advanced International Studies at Johns Hopkins University, told Fox News Digital.

The CRTA Election Observation Mission reported that the campaign was marked by the abuse of state resources, pressure on candidates and voters, attempts to bring the media under total government control, and attacks on independent election observers.
Tens of thousands of Serbians volunteered to run and monitor polling stations across the country, and the vote was mostly peaceful.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio (R) meets with Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York City on September 23, 2025. (Photo by CHARLY TRIBALLEAU / POOL / AFP) (Photo by CHARLY TRIBALLEAU/POOL/AFP via Getty Images) ((Photo by CHARLY TRIBALLEAU/POOL/AFP via Getty Images))
SERBIA, CAUGHT BETWEEN EUROPE AND RUSSIA, COULD MOVE ONE STEP CLOSER TO NORMALIZING RELATIONS WITH KOSOVO

Student led protests marched in the streets for two years after the deaths of 16 people following the collapse of a railway station in the town of Novi Sad in November 2024. People had taken to the streets, demanding justice for those killed and accountability for anyone responsible for the disaster.

The momentum of nearly two years of street demonstrations culminated in a nationwide movement ready for change. The political novices were able to rally the nation behind a simple message against corruption and state capture.

Serbs across the country embraced the Student List, who are viewed as fresh faces in politics and are not tied to Serbia’s traditional political opposition, which is perceived as ineffective and corrupt by a lot of the voters.

Ilija Srdanovic, first on the electoral list "Student List - Students Win" waves to citizens as they welcome students who walked to the capital from different parts of the country a day before their final campaign rally in Belgrade, Serbia, Oct. 21, 2026.  (Marko Djurica/Reuters)
EXCLUSIVE: SERBIAN PRESIDENT VUČIĆ SAYS SUPPORT FOR US 'SURGED' UNDER TRUMP, INVITES HIM TO VISIT BELGRADE
Milos Jevtic, a 48-year-old professor with the Faculty of Organizational Sciences at the University of Belgrade, was among the many Student List candidates who won a seat in parliament.
Jevtic told Fox News Digital that their victory came from the values that the students have stood for from the very beginning: expertise, professionalism, responsibility, solidarity and unity.

"What is particularly important is that the students have never compromised on these values and principles. Of course, widespread public dissatisfaction also played a major role, along with a lack of trust in both the current regime and the opposition parties," Jevtic explained.

Jevtic said he believes the priorities for the new Student List-run government should be economic stability, fighting corruption, establishing the rule of law and strengthening institutions, much of what carried the student-led protests since 2024.

People walk on a bridge with a huge poster of Serbia's former President and the ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) candidate for prime minister Aleksandar Vucic on it, in Nis, Serbia, Oct. 10, 2026. (Marko Djurica/Reuters)
"The ultimate goal is to build a system in which institutions function in the interests of all citizens," Jevtic said.

On foreign policy, there is an expectation that there will be a certain degree of continuity with the Vucic administration in international relations, including maintaining good relations with neighboring European countries and all major international partners.

But Brnabic warned that "Serbia has lost meaningful political pluralism. After 35 years of a multiparty system, the country is effectively left with one established political party, SNS, while the rest of the political scene is dominated by largely unknown movements without a clear ideology. This is catastrophic for any parliamentary democracy."
